The plan fits the budget: it comes to about **14,486 SEK of 15,000**, leaving about 514 SEK. That margin is thin, and the costs behind it aren't firm.

- **Flights and lodging are sample data.** The search tools gave made-up offers, not real availability. Those prices are only for planning, and nothing here can be booked.
- **They came back in US dollars.** I converted them at an assumed 10 SEK to the dollar, which is not today's rate. Each extra 0.5 SEK per dollar adds about 500 SEK to the total.
- **None of the Stockholm research was checked.** The research searches failed, so prices, opening hours, transfers and passes are rough recall, likely from 2023–25. Check before booking:
  - opening hours on Monday 5 July
  - the Vaxholm boat fare
  - whether the 7-day public transport card covers the bus from Bromma airport
  - what the 2027 ID rules are for Amsterdam → Stockholm, if you're not an EU citizen

**Draft plan (sample figures)**
- **Flights:** Anser Airways nonstop, economy, leaving Amsterdam 08:47 Thu 1 Jul for Stockholm Bromma. About 3,162 SEK return.
  - The search didn't return a time for the Monday flight home.
  - Real Amsterdam flights usually land at Arlanda, Stockholm's main airport. The fastest Arlanda nonstop here cost about 2,900 SEK more, which would put the plan over budget.
- **Stay:** a guesthouse rated 9.1 with free cancellation, about 6,854 SEK for 4 nights. The search didn't say which neighbourhood it's in. When you book for real, aim for Södermalm or Norrmalm.
- **Days:**
  - Thu: Gamla Stan (the old town), then a Södermalm viewpoint at sunset
  - Fri: Vasa Museum and Skansen, back by ferry
  - Sat: boat day trip to Vaxholm in the archipelago
  - Sun: City Hall tower, Södermalm and Fotografiska (the photography museum)
  - Mon: a short morning in town, then fly home
- **Other costs:**
  - food: 2,500 SEK (500 a day)
  - 7-day public transport card: 430 SEK
  - sights: 1,040 SEK
  - a 500 SEK buffer
  - The ABBA Museum (about 250–300 SEK) isn't included.

**Cuts if real prices come in higher**
1. Stay in the budget hostel's private room instead. It saves about 1,332 SEK, but it's rated 7.8 and has no free cancellation.
2. Take the one-stop flight to Bromma. It saves about 684 SEK.
3. Skip Fotografiska and the Vaxholm boat and do free Södermalm walks instead. That saves about 570 SEK.

The itinerary is in `/trip/itinerary.md` and the costs are in `/trip/budget.md`. Before booking, search live flight and hotel prices and convert them at the actual exchange rate.

# Stockholm research, 1-5 July 2027 (solo, 4 nights, 15,000 SEK)

Written 2026-11-04.

## READ THIS FIRST: nothing here was verified
- I had no web search or browsing tool in this session. I only had file tools.
- **Every search topic failed.** The topics were: neighbourhoods, attraction hours and prices, ARN and BMA transfers, SL passes, food costs, July weather and events, entry requirements, and Stockholm Pass/Go City.
- Everything below is **recalled from my training data (INFERRED / unverified)**. Nothing was read from a live source.
- Prices are probably 2023-2025 levels. Swedish prices, SL fares and museum prices change most years, usually in January.
- Check every figure on the official site before booking. Sites to check: sl.se, arlandaexpress.se, flygbussarna.se, vasamuseet.se, skansen.se, abbamuseum.com, fotografiska.com, stockholm.se (City Hall), stockholmpass.com, and waxholmsbolaget.se.

## Neighbourhoods (inferred)
- **Norrmalm / City (near T-Centralen):** best for transport links, including the Arlanda Express terminus. It is practical but less charming.
- **Gamla Stan:** the most atmospheric area. Hotels are pricey and it is touristy.
- **Södermalm (SoFo, Mariatorget):** my pick for a solo budget traveller. It has cafés, bars, viewpoints and mid-priced hotels and hostels.
- **Östermalm:** upscale and expensive.
- **Djurgården:** the museum island. Few beds and high prices.
- Hostels and budget options are commonly cited near Centralen and on Södermalm. Examples recalled from memory, not checked: Generator, City Backpackers, and the af Chapman hostel ship.
- Likely cost of 4 nights in July: a hostel dorm is about 350-600 SEK a night. A budget or mid-range hotel is about 1,200-2,200 SEK a night. I have not verified July 2027 rates.

## Attractions (all prices are approximate adult prices, unverified)
| Place | Approx. adult price | July hours (inferred) |
|---|---|---|
| Vasa Museum | ~170-190 SEK | Roughly 08:30-18:00 daily in summer |
| Skansen | ~200-220 SEK in summer | About 10:00-20:00 in summer |
| ABBA The Museum | ~250-300 SEK; timed tickets are advisable | About 10:00-19:00 in summer |
| Fotografiska | ~245-270 SEK | Roughly 09:00-23:00 |
| City Hall (Stadshuset) tower | ~50-60 SEK | Tower open in summer; the tower has been closed at times. Guided tour of the halls is ~130-150 SEK. |
| Gamla Stan, Royal Palace | Walking around is free. Palace ~180-200 SEK. | Palace hours vary by season. |
| Djurgården | Free to walk | Parks and museums nearby, including Junibacken and Gröna Lund. |
| Södermalm viewpoints (Monteliusvägen, Katarinahissen area, Skinnarviksberget) | Free | Always open. |

- **Archipelago day trip:** Fjäderholmarna by boat is about 130-180 SEK return and takes about 25 minutes. Vaxholm by Waxholmsbolaget boat is about 100-200 SEK each way and takes about 1 hour. Vaxholm can also be reached by bus. Summer timetables are fuller. I have not checked the 2027 timetable. SL travel cards are not valid on all Waxholmsbolaget boats. Check this.
- Many museums are closed on Mondays in the off-season. Summer is usually daily. Check the 5 July (Mon) hours for anything you plan to visit.

## Airport transfers (inferred, unverified)
- **Arlanda Express (ARN to Centralen, 18-20 min):** ~330-350 SEK one-way for adults. A return costs more.
- **Commuter train (pendeltåg) and SL:** ~175-200 SEK. This is a single SL ticket plus an airport surcharge. It takes about 40-45 minutes, and the cost is much lower than Arlanda Express.
- **Flygbussarna (airport coach):** ~119-139 SEK one-way online, and takes about 40 minutes.
- **Bromma (BMA):** Flygbussarna runs to Cityterminalen for about 100-120 SEK. The city bus 110 and 15 may also serve it with an SL ticket. I am not certain of the route numbers.
- Amsterdam flights use ARN. KLM, SAS and Norwegian are likely. Check which airport your flight uses, since BMA has had very limited commercial service.

## SL public transport (inferred, unverified)
- Single/90-minute ticket: ~42 SEK.
- 24h: ~165 SEK.
- 72h: ~330 SEK.
- 7-day: ~430 SEK.
- The ferry to Djurgården is included in SL tickets.
- Use the SL app or a contactless card. Paper tickets are not sold.

## Food costs (inferred)
- Budget: ~250-400 SEK a day. This covers a lunch special (dagens lunch) at ~120-150 SEK, supermarket items, and street food.
- Mid-range: ~600-900 SEK a day. A dinner main is about 220-350 SEK.
- Beer at a bar is about 70-95 SEK.

## Stockholm Pass / Go City (inferred)
- The Stockholm Pass (Go City) is about 700-1,000 SEK for 1 day, and about 1,600-2,100 SEK for 3 days. I could not check this.
- It is likely worth it only with 3 or more paid attractions a day. For a balanced itinerary, buying individual tickets is probably cheaper. Do the maths once real prices are confirmed.

## July seasonality (inferred)
- Typical highs are about 20-24°C and lows about 12-14°C. There are roughly 18 hours of daylight, and it is never fully dark.
- Midsummer was in late June. After-effects: Swedes begin 4-5 weeks of holiday in July. Some local restaurants and shops may close or run short hours. Tourist areas stay open. The city feels quiet because locals are away.
- Crowds: July is peak tourist season. Cruise-ship days add crowds to Gamla Stan and Vasa. Book ABBA and Fotografiska ahead.
- Events around 1-5 July 2027: I don't know of any. There may be festivals, and Pride is usually early August. Check the Visit Stockholm events calendar.

## Entry requirements (inferred)
- Amsterdam to Stockholm is an intra-Schengen flight.
- EU/EEA citizens need a valid ID or passport. Non-EU travellers need a valid passport and any visa that applies to their nationality. Carry the passport anyway, since airlines check.
- Sweden can run temporary border checks. The ETIAS system was due to start in late 2026, but its date had slipped before. **Confirm the current ETIAS status for non-EU visa-exempt nationals.** I don't know the traveller's nationality.

## Rough budget check (inferred, 15,000 SEK)
- Lodging 4 nights: 2,000-8,000.
- Transfers and SL: 500-900.
- Attractions: ~1,200-1,800.
- Food: 1,200-3,600.
- Total: roughly 5,000-14,000, so the budget looks workable on these unverified numbers.

# Stockholm — Thu 1 Jul to Mon 5 Jul 2027 (1 traveler, 4 nights)

Flights and lodging below are SAMPLE DATA — illustrative planning figures, not real availability or prices. Search live before booking.
Opening hours and prices are unverified (research searches failed); check official sites, especially Monday hours.

**Flights (sample):** Anser Airways nonstop AMS 08:47 → Stockholm Bromma (BMA), ~4h47 listed duration, economy. Return Mon 5 Jul — return time not returned by the search.
**Stay (sample):** "Quiet guesthouse", 9.1 rating, free cancellation — neighbourhood unknown; aim for Södermalm or Norrmalm when booking for real.
**Transport:** SL 7-day card (~430 SEK) covers metro, buses, trams and some ferries (e.g. Djurgården ferry) — unverified that it covers the Bromma airport bus.

## Day 1 — Thu 1 Jul: Arrive, Gamla Stan
- Morning flight, arrive BMA early afternoon; bus to centre, drop bags
- Afternoon: walk Gamla Stan — Stortorget, Royal Palace exterior, Mårten Trotzigs gränd
- Evening: Monteliusvägen viewpoint on Södermalm at sunset (late, ~22:00), dinner in Söder

## Day 2 — Fri 2 Jul: Djurgården
- Vasa Museum (book timed entry) → Skansen open-air museum (half day)
- Djurgården ferry back from Allmänna gränd to Slussen
- Optional: ABBA Museum (~250–300 SEK, not budgeted)

## Day 3 — Sat 3 Jul: Archipelago day trip
- Boat from Strömkajen to Vaxholm (~1 hr); fortress, waterfront, cinnamon buns
- Return late afternoon; evening in Östermalm / Östermalms saluhall area (check Sat hours)

## Day 4 — Sun 4 Jul: City Hall & Södermalm
- Stockholm City Hall tower climb (seasonal; book on arrival as slots sell out)
- Afternoon: Södermalm — SoFo shops, Skinnarviksberget viewpoint, Fotografiska (open late)

## Day 5 — Mon 5 Jul: Depart
- Morning: Kungsträdgården / Norrmalm, or free Moderna Museet grounds on Skeppsholmen (many museums close Mondays — check)
- Transfer to BMA for return flight (time TBC)

# Stockholm research, 1-5 July 2027 (solo, 4 nights, 15,000 SEK)

Written 2026-11-04.

## READ THIS FIRST: nothing here was verified
- I had no web search or browsing tool in this session. I only had file tools.
- **Every search topic failed.** The topics were: neighbourhoods, attraction hours and prices, ARN and BMA transfers, SL passes, food costs, July weather and events, entry requirements, and Stockholm Pass/Go City.
- Everything below is **recalled from my training data (INFERRED / unverified)**. Nothing was read from a live source.
- Prices are probably 2023-2025 levels. Swedish prices, SL fares and museum prices change most years, usually in January.
- Check every figure on the official site before booking. Sites to check: sl.se, arlandaexpress.se, flygbussarna.se, vasamuseet.se, skansen.se, abbamuseum.com, fotografiska.com, stockholm.se (City Hall), stockholmpass.com, and waxholmsbolaget.se.

## Neighbourhoods (inferred)
- **Norrmalm / City (near T-Centralen):** best for transport links, including the Arlanda Express terminus. It is practical but less charming.
- **Gamla Stan:** the most atmospheric area. Hotels are pricey and it is touristy.
- **Södermalm (SoFo, Mariatorget):** my pick for a solo budget traveller. It has cafés, bars, viewpoints and mid-priced hotels and hostels.
- **Östermalm:** upscale and expensive.
- **Djurgården:** the museum island. Few beds and high prices.
- Hostels and budget options are commonly cited near Centralen and on Södermalm. Examples recalled from memory, not checked: Generator, City Backpackers, and the af Chapman hostel ship.
- Likely cost of 4 nights in July: a hostel dorm is about 350-600 SEK a night. A budget or mid-range hotel is about 1,200-2,200 SEK a night. I have not verified July 2027 rates.

## Attractions (all prices are approximate adult prices, unverified)
| Place | Approx. adult price | July hours (inferred) |
|---|---|---|
| Vasa Museum | ~170-190 SEK | Roughly 08:30-18:00 daily in summer |
| Skansen | ~200-220 SEK in summer | About 10:00-20:00 in summer |
| ABBA The Museum | ~250-300 SEK; timed tickets are advisable | About 10:00-19:00 in summer |
| Fotografiska | ~245-270 SEK | Roughly 09:00-23:00 |
| City Hall (Stadshuset) tower | ~50-60 SEK | Tower open in summer; the tower has been closed at times. Guided tour of the halls is ~130-150 SEK. |
| Gamla Stan, Royal Palace | Walking around is free. Palace ~180-200 SEK. | Palace hours vary by season. |
| Djurgården | Free to walk | Parks and museums nearby, including Junibacken and Gröna Lund. |
| Södermalm viewpoints (Monteliusvägen, Katarinahissen area, Skinnarviksberget) | Free | Always open. |

- **Archipelago day trip:** Fjäderholmarna by boat is about 130-180 SEK return and takes about 25 minutes. Vaxholm by Waxholmsbolaget boat is about 100-200 SEK each way and takes about 1 hour. Vaxholm can also be reached by bus. Summer timetables are fuller. I have not checked the 2027 timetable. SL travel cards are not valid on all Waxholmsbolaget boats. Check this.
- Many museums are closed on Mondays in the off-season. Summer is usually daily. Check the 5 July (Mon) hours for anything you plan to visit.

## Airport transfers (inferred, unverified)
- **Arlanda Express (ARN to Centralen, 18-20 min):** ~330-350 SEK one-way for adults. A return costs more.
- **Commuter train (pendeltåg) and SL:** ~175-200 SEK. This is a single SL ticket plus an airport surcharge. It takes about 40-45 minutes, and the cost is much lower than Arlanda Express.
- **Flygbussarna (airport coach):** ~119-139 SEK one-way online, and takes about 40 minutes.
- **Bromma (BMA):** Flygbussarna runs to Cityterminalen for about 100-120 SEK. The city bus 110 and 15 may also serve it with an SL ticket. I am not certain of the route numbers.
- Amsterdam flights use ARN. KLM, SAS and Norwegian are likely. Check which airport your flight uses, since BMA has had very limited commercial service.

## SL public transport (inferred, unverified)
- Single/90-minute ticket: ~42 SEK.
- 24h: ~165 SEK.
- 72h: ~330 SEK.
- 7-day: ~430 SEK.
- The ferry to Djurgården is included in SL tickets.
- Use the SL app or a contactless card. Paper tickets are not sold.

## Food costs (inferred)
- Budget: ~250-400 SEK a day. This covers a lunch special (dagens lunch) at ~120-150 SEK, supermarket items, and street food.
- Mid-range: ~600-900 SEK a day. A dinner main is about 220-350 SEK.
- Beer at a bar is about 70-95 SEK.

## Stockholm Pass / Go City (inferred)
- The Stockholm Pass (Go City) is about 700-1,000 SEK for 1 day, and about 1,600-2,100 SEK for 3 days. I could not check this.
- It is likely worth it only with 3 or more paid attractions a day. For a balanced itinerary, buying individual tickets is probably cheaper. Do the maths once real prices are confirmed.

## July seasonality (inferred)
- Typical highs are about 20-24°C and lows about 12-14°C. There are roughly 18 hours of daylight, and it is never fully dark.
- Midsummer was in late June. After-effects: Swedes begin 4-5 weeks of holiday in July. Some local restaurants and shops may close or run short hours. Tourist areas stay open. The city feels quiet because locals are away.
- Crowds: July is peak tourist season. Cruise-ship days add crowds to Gamla Stan and Vasa. Book ABBA and Fotografiska ahead.
- Events around 1-5 July 2027: I don't know of any. There may be festivals, and Pride is usually early August. Check the Visit Stockholm events calendar.

## Entry requirements (inferred)
- Amsterdam to Stockholm is an intra-Schengen flight.
- EU/EEA citizens need a valid ID or passport. Non-EU travellers need a valid passport and any visa that applies to their nationality. Carry the passport anyway, since airlines check.
- Sweden can run temporary border checks. The ETIAS system was due to start in late 2026, but its date had slipped before. **Confirm the current ETIAS status for non-EU visa-exempt nationals.** I don't know the traveller's nationality.

## Rough budget check (inferred, 15,000 SEK)
- Lodging 4 nights: 2,000-8,000.
- Transfers and SL: 500-900.
- Attractions: ~1,200-1,800.
- Food: 1,200-3,600.
- Total: roughly 5,000-14,000, so the budget looks workable on these unverified numbers.

# Stockholm — Thu 1 Jul to Mon 5 Jul 2027 (1 traveler, 4 nights)

Flights and lodging below are SAMPLE DATA — illustrative planning figures, not real availability or prices. Search live before booking.
Opening hours and prices are unverified (research searches failed); check official sites, especially Monday hours.

**Flights (sample):** Anser Airways nonstop AMS 08:47 → Stockholm Bromma (BMA), ~4h47 listed duration, economy. Return Mon 5 Jul — return time not returned by the search.
**Stay (sample):** "Quiet guesthouse", 9.1 rating, free cancellation — neighbourhood unknown; aim for Södermalm or Norrmalm when booking for real.
**Transport:** SL 7-day card (~430 SEK) covers metro, buses, trams and some ferries (e.g. Djurgården ferry) — unverified that it covers the Bromma airport bus.

## Day 1 — Thu 1 Jul: Arrive, Gamla Stan
- Morning flight, arrive BMA early afternoon; bus to centre, drop bags
- Afternoon: walk Gamla Stan — Stortorget, Royal Palace exterior, Mårten Trotzigs gränd
- Evening: Monteliusvägen viewpoint on Södermalm at sunset (late, ~22:00), dinner in Söder

## Day 2 — Fri 2 Jul: Djurgården
- Vasa Museum (book timed entry) → Skansen open-air museum (half day)
- Djurgården ferry back from Allmänna gränd to Slussen
- Optional: ABBA Museum (~250–300 SEK, not budgeted)

## Day 3 — Sat 3 Jul: Archipelago day trip
- Boat from Strömkajen to Vaxholm (~1 hr); fortress, waterfront, cinnamon buns
- Return late afternoon; evening in Östermalm / Östermalms saluhall area (check Sat hours)

## Day 4 — Sun 4 Jul: City Hall & Södermalm
- Stockholm City Hall tower climb (seasonal; book on arrival as slots sell out)
- Afternoon: Södermalm — SoFo shops, Skinnarviksberget viewpoint, Fotografiska (open late)

## Day 5 — Mon 5 Jul: Depart
- Morning: Kungsträdgården / Norrmalm, or free Moderna Museet grounds on Skeppsholmen (many museums close Mondays — check)

# Kyoto research, 5–10 Apr 2027 (2 adults, SFO→KIX, $4,000 total)

## READ THIS FIRST: provenance
**I had no web search or fetch tool in this session. Only file tools.** Nothing below was read from a live source or verified. Everything is from my background knowledge (training data, roughly through 2025). All of it is **UNVERIFIED and may be stale**. Today is 4 Nov 2026. Fares, fees, taxes and passes in Japan changed a lot in 2024–2026. Re-check every item marked ⚠ before booking.

**Failed searches (none could run), by topic:** (1) 2027 cherry blossom forecast and hanami spots; (2) attraction fees and hours; (3) neighbourhoods and hotel prices; (4) KIX–Kyoto fares and local transport passes; (5) Nara day trip costs; (6) food costs; (7) entry rules (JESTA, Visit Japan Web) and April 2027 closures or renovations; (8) Kyoto accommodation tax and departure tax.

Exchange rate assumption (inferred, not checked): about ¥150 = $1. Re-check it.

## 1. Cherry blossom (inferred from memory of past years)
- Kyoto full bloom (mankai) has recently fallen between about 25 Mar and 5 Apr. Examples I recall: 2021 about 26 Mar, 2023 about 25 Mar, 2024 about 3–4 Apr, 2025 about 5 Apr. Trend: earlier than the old average of about 5 Apr.
- **Inference:** 5–10 Apr 2027 will probably fall at or just after peak, in the petal-fall (hanafubuki) stage. That is still pretty, and crowds are usually a little thinner than at peak. Timing is uncertain by about ±1 week. JMC and Japan Weather Association forecasts start in January–February 2027, so check them then. Book hotels with free cancellation.
- Spots I remember (not verified for 2027):
  - Philosopher's Path (Higashiyama): free.
  - Maruyama Park (Gion): free, with a famous weeping cherry.
  - Kamo River bank (Demachiyanagi to Kitaoji): free and quiet.
  - Arashiyama / Hirosawa Pond.
  - Daigo-ji: fee about ¥1,500 or more in the blossom season (⚠), further out at Yamashina.
  - Heian Shrine garden: about ¥600–700.
  - Ninna-ji: late-blooming Omuro cherries, usually mid to late April. This is a good fallback if the main bloom is over.
  - Kyoto Botanical Garden.
- Crowd avoidance (general advice, inferred): go to Fushimi Inari, Kiyomizu-dera, and the Arashiyama bamboo grove before 7:30. Do Gion and Higashiyama at dawn. Use weekdays. 5 Apr is a Monday and 10 Apr is a Saturday, so keep the weekend for lower-traffic areas such as the Kamo River or Nara. Late-blooming Omuro and the northern hills are good fallbacks.

## 2. Attractions (⚠ all fees and hours unverified; check official sites)
| Area | Site | Fee (¥) | Hours / closed days (recalled) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Higashiyama | Kiyomizu-dera | about 500 | About 6:00–18:00. Evening openings in spring. Usually no regular closed day. |
| Higashiyama | Yasaka Shrine, Gion streets, Hanamikoji | Free | Open 24h. Do not enter private alleys. Photography restrictions apply in Gion. |
| Higashiyama | Ginkaku-ji | about 500 | About 8:30–17:00 |
| Higashiyama | Kodai-ji, Kennin-ji | About 600 / 500 | Roughly 9:00–17:00 |
| Arashiyama | Bamboo grove | Free | Open 24h; crowded after 9:00 |
| Arashiyama | Tenryu-ji garden | about 500 (+300 for buildings) | About 8:30–17:00 |
| Arashiyama | Monkey Park Iwatayama | about 800 | About 9:00–16:30 |
| Fushimi Inari | Taisha and torii trail | Free | Open 24h. Go before 8:00 or after 17:00. |
| North | Kinkaku-ji | about 500 | About 9:00–17:00, open daily |
| North | Ryoan-ji | about 600 | About 8:00–17:00 |
| North | Nijo Castle | ⚠ 800, possibly raised to about 1,300 | About 8:45–16:00. Closed some Tuesdays in Dec/Jan/Jul/Aug, not April (unverified). |
| Central | Nishiki Market | Free to enter | Most stalls about 10:00–17:00; some close Wednesdays. |
| Central | Kyoto Imperial Palace grounds | Free | Closed Mondays (⚠ check) |

## 3. Where to stay (mostly inferred)
- Best value and access: around Kyoto Station (JR, subway, Haruka, Nara line), Shijo-Karasuma / Kawaramachi (central, walkable to Nishiki and Gion), and Gojo / Shichijo (cheaper hostels and business hotels).
- Typical budget room prices: ¥8,000–15,000 a night in a normal week, probably ¥15,000–30,000 or more in blossom week. Book early. Do not rely on these figures; they are my guess.
- Cheaper alternative: stay in Osaka (Shin-Osaka, Namba) and commute. Kyoto is about 30 minutes by Shinkansen or about 50 minutes by JR Special Rapid. Hotels there are often cheaper.
- Budget inference: 5 nights at ¥15,000–20,000 comes to about ¥75,000–100,000 (about $500–670).

## 4. Transport (⚠ unverified)
- **KIX→Kyoto Station**
  - JR Haruka: about 75–80 min. Recalled standard fare about ¥3,000 non-reserved and about ¥3,600 reserved. Foreign-visitor discounted tickets (about ¥2,200–2,500) were sold online or at the airport. Check the current JR-West price.
  - Limousine bus: about 90–105 min, about ¥2,800–3,000. Traffic can delay it.
  - Cheapest: JR Kansai Airport Rapid to Osaka, then transfer. This is slower and not worth it with luggage.
- **Local**
  - City bus is a flat fare of about ¥230. Buses are crowded in blossom season.
  - The Kyoto bus-only day pass was **discontinued in 2024** (my recollection). A subway-only day pass exists (about ¥800–1,100, ⚠ price may have changed). Check whether any new tourist pass has replaced it.
  - Use an IC card (ICOCA, Suica or Pasmo) for buses, subway and trains. Mobile Suica/ICOCA in Apple Wallet works on iPhone. Physical ICOCA sales were restricted at times in 2023–2025, so check availability.
  - JR Nara line and Keihan/Hankyu cover Fushimi Inari (JR Inari station, 5 min from Kyoto Station, about ¥150), Arashiyama (JR Sagano line, about ¥240) and Gion (Keihan Gion-Shijo).
  - Walk and use trains over buses where possible to save money and avoid crowds.

## 5. Day trip: Nara (⚠)
- From Kyoto: JR Miyakoji Rapid about 45 min, about ¥720–760. Kintetsu limited express about 35–45 min, about ¥760 with surcharge-free express (check).
- Costs: Nara Park free; Todai-ji about ¥800; Kasuga Taisha outer area free, inner about ¥500; deer crackers about ¥200.
- Total per person is about ¥2,500–3,500 including transport and entry fees, excluding lunch.
- Alternative: Fushimi Inari combined with Uji (Byodo-in about ¥700) is cheaper.

## 6. Food (inferred)
- Budget (per person per day): ¥3,000–4,500, using konbini breakfast (¥300–600), lunch sets and ramen / udon / gyudon (¥800–1,200), dinner at an izakaya or conveyor-belt sushi (¥1,200–2,000).
- Mid-range: ¥6,000–10,000. Tipping is not customary.
- For two, over 6 days: budget about ¥54,000–80,000 (about $360–530).

## 7. Entry requirements and closures
- Recalled: US citizens can enter visa-free for up to 90 days as tourists. They need a passport valid for the stay. Check whether anything changed.
- Visit Japan Web (immigration, customs and tax-free pre-registration) is optional but speeds arrival. Register before travel.
- **JESTA** (Japan's planned ESTA-style pre-travel authorization): as I recall, it was announced with an intended launch around fiscal 2028. **I could not confirm it will be required by April 2027. Treat as unconfirmed and check the Japanese MOFA / MOJ site before booking.**
- Closures or renovations in April 2027: **unknown.** I have no verified information. Check each temple's official site, and check Kiyomizu-dera, Nishi Hongan-ji, Nijo Castle and Kinkaku-ji for events or maintenance.

## 8. Taxes and fees (⚠ unverified)
- Kyoto accommodation tax: previously ¥200–1,000 per person per night depending on room price. **Kyoto approved a large increase, planned from about March 2026**, with tiers of roughly ¥200 under ¥6,000 per person, ¥400 for ¥6,000–19,999, up to ¥10,000 for the most expensive rooms. Verify the tiers; budget hotels should be about ¥200–400 per person per night.
- Japan's departure tax (international tourist tax) was ¥1,000 and is included in airfare. I recall a plan to raise it to about ¥3,000 from July 2026. Check whether it is in your ticket; it is not normally charged separately.
- Consumption tax is 10%. Tax-free shopping is available for tourists; I do not know the 2026 rule changes (a refund-based system is planned from Nov 2026).

## Budget sketch (inferred; flights are the swing factor)
- Flights SFO–KIX in April blossom season: I have no live prices. My guess is about $900–1,400 each, so $1,800–2,800 for two. **This could consume most of the $4,000.**
- Ground budget (6 nights): lodging about $500–900 + food $360–530 + transport about $150 + attractions about $100 + Nara about $50 = about $1,200–1,800.
- Total is probably about $3,000–4,600. It is tight but possible if flights are ≤ about $1,000 each. Check airfare first, and consider flying into Osaka Itami or Tokyo only if cheaper (that changes the plan).

Risk: real airfares and hotel rates during cherry-blossom week are likely higher than these sample figures. The ~$1,085 headroom is the buffer for that.

# Kyoto — 2 adults, 5–10 April 2027

**Base:** Kyoto Station guesthouse, 4 nights (6–10 Apr). It is sample-data, so this stands for the type of place to look for, not a specific listing.
**Flights:** SFO→KIX, 1 stop, economy, Blue Corridor. Also sample-data: leaves SFO 5 Apr at 15:56 and arrives 6 Apr local time.
**Est. total:** $2,914.94 of $4,000 (see budget.md).

Important: none of the research below was checked against a live source, because web search was unavailable. Fees, opening hours, fares, bloom timing and entry rules are all background knowledge and need confirming before you travel.

---

## Mon 5 Apr — Depart
- Afternoon flight SFO→KIX. You cross the date line, so you land on 6 Apr.

## Tue 6 Apr — Arrive Kyoto
- Land at KIX. Take the JR Haruka to Kyoto Station: about 75 min and about ¥3,000 (unconfirmed). Buy IC cards (ICOCA) at the airport.
- Check in near Kyoto Station.
- Easy evening: dinner at Kyoto Station / Porta, then the view from the Kyoto Tower area. Early night.

## Wed 7 Apr — Fushimi Inari + Higashiyama (blossom day)
- **Before 8:00:** Fushimi Inari. It's 5 min on the JR Nara line, and free. Walk up to the Yotsutsuji viewpoint, about 1.5–2 h round trip.
- **Late morning:** Kiyomizu-dera (about ¥500, unconfirmed), then down Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka.
- **Afternoon:** Kodai-ji, then Maruyama Park (its weeping cherry is a classic hanami spot), then Yasaka Shrine.
- **Evening:** Shirakawa canal and Hanamikoji in Gion. The canal is lit up in blossom season (unconfirmed for 2027). Dinner around Pontocho or Kawaramachi.

## Thu 8 Apr — Arashiyama + northwest
- **Early (by 8:00):** JR Sagano line to Saga-Arashiyama. Bamboo grove (free), then Tenryu-ji garden (about ¥500, unconfirmed).
- Togetsukyo Bridge and the riverbank cherries, then lunch in Arashiyama.
- **Afternoon:** bus or taxi to Ninna-ji, whose late-blooming Omuro cherries are the best bet if the main bloom has passed. Then Ryoan-ji, then Kinkaku-ji (about ¥500 each, unconfirmed).
- **Evening:** back to the station area. Optional tea ceremony (budgeted at $50 for 2).

## Fri 9 Apr — Nara day trip + Philosopher's Path
- **Morning:** Kintetsu or JR to Nara, about 45 min. Nara Park deer, Todai-ji (about ¥800, unconfirmed), Kasuga Taisha.
- Return by mid-afternoon.
- **Late afternoon:** Philosopher's Path, the canal lined with cherry trees, from Ginkaku-ji (about ¥500, unconfirmed) south toward Nanzen-ji.
- **Evening:** Nishiki Market closes early (around 17:00–18:00, unconfirmed), so if you want it, go before the Path. Farewell dinner.

## Sat 10 Apr — Depart
- Check out. Haruka to KIX, leaving at least 3 h before departure.
- If your flight is in the evening, spend the morning at Nishiki Market or To-ji (five-storey pagoda, near the station).
- You land in SFO the same calendar day.

---

## Confirm before booking / travelling (all unchecked)
- **Bloom forecast.** Peak usually falls in late March to early April, so these dates may catch the end of it. Forecasts come out around Jan–Feb 2027. Book lodging with free cancellation.
- **Entry rules for US citizens.** Visa-free entry for up to 90 days and Visit Japan Web are unconfirmed. Whether JESTA pre-travel authorisation will be required by April 2027 is also unconfirmed.
- **Costs and hours.** Kyoto accommodation tax rate, Haruka fare and any tourist discount, bus fares (the bus day pass is believed to have been discontinued), temple fees and hours.
- **Closures.** Any April 2027 closures or renovations at the sites above.

**Flights, round trip for 2 (all sample-data):**
- **Cheapest:** Anser Airways SFO–KIX with 2 stops, $1,320.36 total.
- **Most convenient:** Northwind SFO–KIX nonstop, $1,917.44 total. It departs at 10:49 and is the cheapest nonstop. Meridian Air is also nonstop but costs $2,055.44, slightly over your $2,000 flight target.
- **Middle option:** Blue Corridor with 1 stop, $1,409.18.
- **ITM:** The prices are similar ($1,349.88 to $2,101.52) and give no real advantage, so KIX is the better choice.

**Lodging, 4 nights for 2 (all sample-data):**
- **Cheapest:** Kyoto Station private-room hostel, $492.28. It has no free cancellation.
- **Best value:** Kyoto Station guesthouse, $598.76. It is rated 9.1 and has free cancellation.
- **More convenient and pricier:**
  - Kyoto Station central boutique hotel: $934.20, no free cancellation.
  - Gion riverside apartment: $990.60, free cancellation.
  - Gion central boutique hotel: $1,143.00, over your lodging target.

I didn't search Shijo/Kawaramachi separately. The Gion results are the closest stand-in.

**Combined flights and lodging for 2:**

| Scenario | Flights | Lodging | Total | Left for everything else |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cheapest | Anser, 2 stops | Kyoto Station hostel | $1,812.64 | about $2,187 |
| Good value | Blue Corridor, 1 stop | Kyoto Station guesthouse | $2,007.94 | about $1,992 |
| Most convenient | Northwind nonstop | Kyoto Station boutique hotel | $2,851.64 | about $1,148 |

**Tradeoff:** The most convenient option costs about $1,040 more than the cheapest. You get a nonstop flight instead of 2 stops and a better-located, better-rated stay. It leaves roughly half as much for food, transport and activities.

The Gion boutique hotel with the nonstop flight totals $3,060.44, which leaves only about $940. The 1-stop flight with the guesthouse is the best balance if you want to keep the budget intact.

I couldn't research this properly. I had no web search or browsing tool, only file tools. `/trip/research.md` is written from my background knowledge (roughly through 2025) and **none of it is verified**. Every fee, fare, hour and tax should be re-checked.

**Searches that failed, by topic:** bloom forecast and hanami spots, attraction fees and hours, neighbourhoods and hotel prices, KIX–Kyoto fares and local passes, Nara costs, food costs, entry rules (JESTA, Visit Japan Web), April 2027 closures, and Kyoto and departure taxes.

The four things that most affect the plan, all unverified:
1. **Bloom timing:** Kyoto's peak bloom has recently fallen between about 25 March and 5 April. Your dates of 5–10 April will probably be at or just after peak, in the petal-fall stage. Official forecasts won't appear until about January–February 2027. Book hotels with free cancellation. Ninna-ji's late-blooming cherries are a fallback.
2. **Budget:** flights are the big unknown. I had no live prices, and my guess is $900–1,400 each. The on-the-ground costs are about $1,200–1,800 for six nights, using these figures (¥150 = $1, not checked):
   - Hotels: roughly ¥15,000–20,000 a night in blossom week.
   - Food: ¥3,000–4,500 per person per day.
   - Temple entry fees: mostly ¥500–800.
   - Nara day trip: about ¥2,500–3,500 per person.

   Check airfare first. The $4,000 total only works if flights come in at about $1,000 each or less.
3. **Transport:**
   - **KIX to Kyoto:** the Haruka train is about ¥3,000 (discounted tourist tickets of about ¥2,200–2,500 may exist). The limousine bus is about ¥2,800–3,000. Both take roughly 75–100 minutes.
   - **Kyoto buses:** the flat fare is about ¥230. I believe the city's bus day pass was discontinued in 2024, so use an IC card.
   - **Free sights:** Fushimi Inari and the Arashiyama bamboo grove are free. Go before 8:00 to avoid crowds.
4. **Rules and taxes:**
   - **Entry:** US citizens should be visa-free for 90 days, and Visit Japan Web is optional. I couldn't confirm whether JESTA, Japan's planned pre-travel authorization, will be required by April 2027. As I recall it was planned for around 2028, so check the Japanese government site.
   - **Kyoto accommodation tax:** I believe it was raised significantly from about March 2026. It should be about ¥200–400 per person per night for budget rooms.
   - **Departure tax:** the ¥1,000 tax is included in the airfare, and I recall a planned rise to about ¥3,000.
   - **Closures:** I found nothing on April 2027 closures or renovations, so check each site before you go.

# Kyoto research, 5–10 Apr 2027 (2 adults, SFO→KIX, $4,000 total)

## READ THIS FIRST: provenance
**I had no web search or fetch tool in this session. Only file tools.** Nothing below was read from a live source or verified. Everything is from my background knowledge (training data, roughly through 2025). All of it is **UNVERIFIED and may be stale**. Today is 4 Nov 2026. Fares, fees, taxes and passes in Japan changed a lot in 2024–2026. Re-check every item marked ⚠ before booking.

**Failed searches (none could run), by topic:** (1) 2027 cherry blossom forecast and hanami spots; (2) attraction fees and hours; (3) neighbourhoods and hotel prices; (4) KIX–Kyoto fares and local transport passes; (5) Nara day trip costs; (6) food costs; (7) entry rules (JESTA, Visit Japan Web) and April 2027 closures or renovations; (8) Kyoto accommodation tax and departure tax.

Exchange rate assumption (inferred, not checked): about ¥150 = $1. Re-check it.

## 1. Cherry blossom (inferred from memory of past years)
- Kyoto full bloom (mankai) has recently fallen between about 25 Mar and 5 Apr. Examples I recall: 2021 about 26 Mar, 2023 about 25 Mar, 2024 about 3–4 Apr, 2025 about 5 Apr. Trend: earlier than the old average of about 5 Apr.
- **Inference:** 5–10 Apr 2027 will probably fall at or just after peak, in the petal-fall (hanafubuki) stage. That is still pretty, and crowds are usually a little thinner than at peak. Timing is uncertain by about ±1 week. JMC and Japan Weather Association forecasts start in January–February 2027, so check them then. Book hotels with free cancellation.
- Spots I remember (not verified for 2027):
  - Philosopher's Path (Higashiyama): free.
  - Maruyama Park (Gion): free, with a famous weeping cherry.
  - Kamo River bank (Demachiyanagi to Kitaoji): free and quiet.
  - Arashiyama / Hirosawa Pond.
  - Daigo-ji: fee about ¥1,500 or more in the blossom season (⚠), further out at Yamashina.
  - Heian Shrine garden: about ¥600–700.
  - Ninna-ji: late-blooming Omuro cherries, usually mid to late April. This is a good fallback if the main bloom is over.
  - Kyoto Botanical Garden.
- Crowd avoidance (general advice, inferred): go to Fushimi Inari, Kiyomizu-dera, and the Arashiyama bamboo grove before 7:30. Do Gion and Higashiyama at dawn. Use weekdays. 5 Apr is a Monday and 10 Apr is a Saturday, so keep the weekend for lower-traffic areas such as the Kamo River or Nara. Late-blooming Omuro and the northern hills are good fallbacks.

## 2. Attractions (⚠ all fees and hours unverified; check official sites)
| Area | Site | Fee (¥) | Hours / closed days (recalled) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Higashiyama | Kiyomizu-dera | about 500 | About 6:00–18:00. Evening openings in spring. Usually no regular closed day. |
| Higashiyama | Yasaka Shrine, Gion streets, Hanamikoji | Free | Open 24h. Do not enter private alleys. Photography restrictions apply in Gion. |
| Higashiyama | Ginkaku-ji | about 500 | About 8:30–17:00 |
| Higashiyama | Kodai-ji, Kennin-ji | About 600 / 500 | Roughly 9:00–17:00 |
| Arashiyama | Bamboo grove | Free | Open 24h; crowded after 9:00 |
| Arashiyama | Tenryu-ji garden | about 500 (+300 for buildings) | About 8:30–17:00 |
| Arashiyama | Monkey Park Iwatayama | about 800 | About 9:00–16:30 |
| Fushimi Inari | Taisha and torii trail | Free | Open 24h. Go before 8:00 or after 17:00. |
| North | Kinkaku-ji | about 500 | About 9:00–17:00, open daily |
| North | Ryoan-ji | about 600 | About 8:00–17:00 |
| North | Nijo Castle | ⚠ 800, possibly raised to about 1,300 | About 8:45–16:00. Closed some Tuesdays in Dec/Jan/Jul/Aug, not April (unverified). |
| Central | Nishiki Market | Free to enter | Most stalls about 10:00–17:00; some close Wednesdays. |
| Central | Kyoto Imperial Palace grounds | Free | Closed Mondays (⚠ check) |

## 3. Where to stay (mostly inferred)
- Best value and access: around Kyoto Station (JR, subway, Haruka, Nara line), Shijo-Karasuma / Kawaramachi (central, walkable to Nishiki and Gion), and Gojo / Shichijo (cheaper hostels and business hotels).
- Typical budget room prices: ¥8,000–15,000 a night in a normal week, probably ¥15,000–30,000 or more in blossom week. Book early. Do not rely on these figures; they are my guess.
- Cheaper alternative: stay in Osaka (Shin-Osaka, Namba) and commute. Kyoto is about 30 minutes by Shinkansen or about 50 minutes by JR Special Rapid. Hotels there are often cheaper.
- Budget inference: 5 nights at ¥15,000–20,000 comes to about ¥75,000–100,000 (about $500–670).

## 4. Transport (⚠ unverified)
- **KIX→Kyoto Station**
  - JR Haruka: about 75–80 min. Recalled standard fare about ¥3,000 non-reserved and about ¥3,600 reserved. Foreign-visitor discounted tickets (about ¥2,200–2,500) were sold online or at the airport. Check the current JR-West price.
  - Limousine bus: about 90–105 min, about ¥2,800–3,000. Traffic can delay it.
  - Cheapest: JR Kansai Airport Rapid to Osaka, then transfer. This is slower and not worth it with luggage.
- **Local**
  - City bus is a flat fare of about ¥230. Buses are crowded in blossom season.
  - The Kyoto bus-only day pass was **discontinued in 2024** (my recollection). A subway-only day pass exists (about ¥800–1,100, ⚠ price may have changed). Check whether any new tourist pass has replaced it.
  - Use an IC card (ICOCA, Suica or Pasmo) for buses, subway and trains. Mobile Suica/ICOCA in Apple Wallet works on iPhone. Physical ICOCA sales were restricted at times in 2023–2025, so check availability.
  - JR Nara line and Keihan/Hankyu cover Fushimi Inari (JR Inari station, 5 min from Kyoto Station, about ¥150), Arashiyama (JR Sagano line, about ¥240) and Gion (Keihan Gion-Shijo).
  - Walk and use trains over buses where possible to save money and avoid crowds.

## 5. Day trip: Nara (⚠)
- From Kyoto: JR Miyakoji Rapid about 45 min, about ¥720–760. Kintetsu limited express about 35–45 min, about ¥760 with surcharge-free express (check).
- Costs: Nara Park free; Todai-ji about ¥800; Kasuga Taisha outer area free, inner about ¥500; deer crackers about ¥200.
- Total per person is about ¥2,500–3,500 including transport and entry fees, excluding lunch.
- Alternative: Fushimi Inari combined with Uji (Byodo-in about ¥700) is cheaper.

## 6. Food (inferred)
- Budget (per person per day): ¥3,000–4,500, using konbini breakfast (¥300–600), lunch sets and ramen / udon / gyudon (¥800–1,200), dinner at an izakaya or conveyor-belt sushi (¥1,200–2,000).
- Mid-range: ¥6,000–10,000. Tipping is not customary.
- For two, over 6 days: budget about ¥54,000–80,000 (about $360–530).

## 7. Entry requirements and closures
- Recalled: US citizens can enter visa-free for up to 90 days as tourists. They need a passport valid for the stay. Check whether anything changed.
- Visit Japan Web (immigration, customs and tax-free pre-registration) is optional but speeds arrival. Register before travel.
- **JESTA** (Japan's planned ESTA-style pre-travel authorization): as I recall, it was announced with an intended launch around fiscal 2028. **I could not confirm it will be required by April 2027. Treat as unconfirmed and check the Japanese MOFA / MOJ site before booking.**
- Closures or renovations in April 2027: **unknown.** I have no verified information. Check each temple's official site, and check Kiyomizu-dera, Nishi Hongan-ji, Nijo Castle and Kinkaku-ji for events or maintenance.

## 8. Taxes and fees (⚠ unverified)
- Kyoto accommodation tax: previously ¥200–1,000 per person per night depending on room price. **Kyoto approved a large increase, planned from about March 2026**, with tiers of roughly ¥200 under ¥6,000 per person, ¥400 for ¥6,000–19,999, up to ¥10,000 for the most expensive rooms. Verify the tiers; budget hotels should be about ¥200–400 per person per night.
- Japan's departure tax (international tourist tax) was ¥1,000 and is included in airfare. I recall a plan to raise it to about ¥3,000 from July 2026. Check whether it is in your ticket; it is not normally charged separately.
- Consumption tax is 10%. Tax-free shopping is available for tourists; I do not know the 2026 rule changes (a refund-based system is planned from Nov 2026).

## Budget sketch (inferred; flights are the swing factor)
- Flights SFO–KIX in April blossom season: I have no live prices. My guess is about $900–1,400 each, so $1,800–2,800 for two. **This could consume most of the $4,000.**
- Ground budget (6 nights): lodging about $500–900 + food $360–530 + transport about $150 + attractions about $100 + Nara about $50 = about $1,200–1,800.
- Total is probably about $3,000–4,600. It is tight but possible if flights are ≤ about $1,000 each. Check airfare first, and consider flying into Osaka Itami or Tokyo only if cheaper (that changes the plan).

# Kyoto — 2 adults, 5–10 April 2027

**Base:** Kyoto Station guesthouse, 4 nights (6–10 Apr). It is sample-data, so this stands for the type of place to look for, not a specific listing.
**Flights:** SFO→KIX, 1 stop, economy, Blue Corridor. Also sample-data: leaves SFO 5 Apr at 15:56 and arrives 6 Apr local time.
**Est. total:** $2,914.94 of $4,000 (see budget.md).

Important: none of the research below was checked against a live source, because web search was unavailable. Fees, opening hours, fares, bloom timing and entry rules are all background knowledge and need confirming before you travel.

---

## Mon 5 Apr — Depart
- Afternoon flight SFO→KIX. You cross the date line, so you land on 6 Apr.

## Tue 6 Apr — Arrive Kyoto
- Land at KIX. Take the JR Haruka to Kyoto Station: about 75 min and about ¥3,000 (unconfirmed). Buy IC cards (ICOCA) at the airport.
- Check in near Kyoto Station.
- Easy evening: dinner at Kyoto Station / Porta, then the view from the Kyoto Tower area. Early night.

## Wed 7 Apr — Fushimi Inari + Higashiyama (blossom day)
- **Before 8:00:** Fushimi Inari. It's 5 min on the JR Nara line, and free. Walk up to the Yotsutsuji viewpoint, about 1.5–2 h round trip.
- **Late morning:** Kiyomizu-dera (about ¥500, unconfirmed), then down Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka.
- **Afternoon:** Kodai-ji, then Maruyama Park (its weeping cherry is a classic hanami spot), then Yasaka Shrine.
- **Evening:** Shirakawa canal and Hanamikoji in Gion. The canal is lit up in blossom season (unconfirmed for 2027). Dinner around Pontocho or Kawaramachi.

## Thu 8 Apr — Arashiyama + northwest
- **Early (by 8:00):** JR Sagano line to Saga-Arashiyama. Bamboo grove (free), then Tenryu-ji garden (about ¥500, unconfirmed).
- Togetsukyo Bridge and the riverbank cherries, then lunch in Arashiyama.
- **Afternoon:** bus or taxi to Ninna-ji, whose late-blooming Omuro cherries are the best bet if the main bloom has passed. Then Ryoan-ji, then Kinkaku-ji (about ¥500 each, unconfirmed).
- **Evening:** back to the station area. Optional tea ceremony (budgeted at $50 for 2).

## Fri 9 Apr — Nara day trip + Philosopher's Path
- **Morning:** Kintetsu or JR to Nara, about 45 min. Nara Park deer, Todai-ji (about ¥800, unconfirmed), Kasuga Taisha.
- Return by mid-afternoon.
- **Late afternoon:** Philosopher's Path, the canal lined with cherry trees, from Ginkaku-ji (about ¥500, unconfirmed) south toward Nanzen-ji.
- **Evening:** Nishiki Market closes early (around 17:00–18:00, unconfirmed), so if you want it, go before the Path. Farewell dinner.

## Sat 10 Apr — Depart
- Check out. Haruka to KIX, leaving at least 3 h before departure.
- If your flight is in the evening, spend the morning at Nishiki Market or To-ji (five-storey pagoda, near the station).
- You land in SFO the same calendar day.

---

## Confirm before booking / travelling (all unchecked)
- **Bloom forecast.** Peak usually falls in late March to early April, so these dates may catch the end of it. Forecasts come out around Jan–Feb 2027. Book lodging with free cancellation.
- **Entry rules for US citizens.** Visa-free entry for up to 90 days and Visit Japan Web are unconfirmed. Whether JESTA pre-travel authorisation will be required by April 2027 is also unconfirmed.
- **Costs and hours.** Kyoto accommodation tax rate, Haruka fare and any tourist discount, bus fares (the bus day pass is believed to have been discontinued), temple fees and hours.
- **Closures.** Any April 2027 closures or renovations at the sites above.

# Rome research, 1-4 Dec 2026 (Tue-Fri), solo first-timer from Boston

## IMPORTANT LIMITATION
This session had no web search or web fetch tool, only file tools. **Nothing below was verified against a live source today (4 Nov 2026).** Everything is from my background knowledge (training data, roughly up to 2024-25) and is labelled INFERRED/RECALLED. Prices, hours and schemes may have changed. Check every item against the official sites before booking.

Failed searches (all of them, because no search tool was available): opening hours and booking rules for all attractions, Dec 2026 events and strikes, weather, FCO transfers, neighbourhoods, transit prices, food costs.

## Calendar for the trip (verified by calendar arithmetic)
- Tue 1 Dec, Wed 2 Dec, Thu 3 Dec, Fri 4 Dec 2026.
- The last Sunday of November is 29 Nov, before the trip. The free or open-Sunday Vatican day does not apply. No Sunday or Monday falls in the trip, so **the Borghese Monday closure and the Vatican Sunday closure do not affect these dates**.

## 1. Attractions (RECALLED, UNVERIFIED)
- **Colosseum / Forum / Palatine**: A combined timed ticket (the "Full Experience" and standard tickets) is sold at parcocolosseo.it. Typically open daily from about 9:00 until about 1 hour before sunset, which is around 16:30-17:00 in December. It is closed 25 Dec and 1 Jan. Tickets were about €18 for the standard combo, and prices have been rising. Names are on tickets and ID is checked. Book weeks ahead. Dec is low season, so slots are easier, but book now. Tickets are valid 24h for a one-time entry to each site.
- **Vatican Museums + Sistine Chapel**: Open Mon-Sat, about 9:00-18:00 with last entry around 16:00. Closed Sundays except the last Sunday of the month. Standard ticket about €20 plus a €5 online reservation fee. Book at tickets.museivaticani.va. Closed on religious holidays, including 8 Dec (outside the trip). I know of no closure on 1-4 Dec, but check the official calendar. Wednesday mornings (papal audience) make St Peter's Square busy, and the Basilica may be restricted. 2 Dec is a Wednesday.
- **St Peter's Basilica**: Free entry, with an optional free timed "fast track" reservation. Open about 7:00-19:00 (until about 18:30 in winter). It can close for papal ceremonies. A security queue is likely. Dress code: shoulders and knees covered. Dome climb about €8-10 by stairs or €10-15 by lift. Wednesday audience mornings can restrict access.
- **Pantheon**: Since July 2023 it has been ticketed for non-residents at about €5. Open about 9:00-19:00. Tickets are bought on site or online. Mass is held on Sat evening and Sun morning, outside the trip. Confirm the current price and booking rules.
- **Borghese Gallery**: Reservation is mandatory, with timed 2-hour slots. Open Tue-Sun, closed Monday. Ticket about €15 plus a fee, and it often sells out days ahead. Book at galleriaborghese.it. All trip days are open days, but 1 Dec is the arrival day, so Wed 2 Dec to Fri 4 Dec is better.
- **Trevi Fountain**: Free to view. In Feb 2024 the city said it would introduce a charge. In Jan 2026 I do not know the outcome. I recall a plan for a roughly €2 fee for tourists from early 2026, and I could not confirm it. **Verify.** Visit early morning or late evening to avoid crowds.
- Other first-timer picks (not researched): Spanish Steps, Piazza Navona, Campo de' Fiori, Castel Sant'Angelo, Trastevere in the evening, Capitoline Museums, Appian Way.

## 2. Holidays, events and strikes, 1-4 Dec (RECALLED, UNVERIFIED)
- No national holiday falls on 1-4 Dec. 8 Dec (Immaculate Conception) is a holiday after the trip. The Pope usually visits the Spanish Steps that day, and the area closes then.
- Christmas markets: Piazza Navona's market usually opens in early December, or sometimes on the first weekend of Dec (tends to open around 6-8 Dec and run to 6 Jan). Start dates for 2026 are unconfirmed, and it may not be open by 4 Dec. The Christmas tree and lights usually go up in early December.
- 2025-26 Jubilee has ended. Crowds should be lower than in 2025.
- Strikes (scioperi): Italy has frequent transit strikes, often on Fridays and often announced 10-15 days ahead. Check the Italian ministry's strike calendar (scioperi.mit.gov.it) for 4 Dec, which is a Friday and also your departure day. Allow extra time for the airport.

## 3. Weather and daylight (RECALLED, UNVERIFIED)
- Early December: highs about 13-14°C, lows about 5-6°C. It is wet, with about 8-10 rainy days in the month. Pack a rain jacket, layers and an umbrella.
- Sunrise about 7:15, sunset about 16:40-16:45. About 9.5 hours of daylight. Plan outdoor sites before sunset.

## 4. Airport transfer FCO to the centre (RECALLED, UNVERIFIED)
- Leonardo Express to Roma Termini: non-stop, about 32 minutes, running about every 15 minutes from about 6:23 until about 23:23. Fare was €14 (raised from €14 in 2023). Verify the fare.
- Regional train FL1 to Trastevere, Ostiense and Tiburtina: about €8, slower, cheaper.
- Fixed taxi fare from FCO to inside the Aurelian Walls: €50 (including luggage and up to 4 passengers) since 2023. Use only official white taxis. Verify.
- Shuttle buses (Terravision, SIT) at about €6-7 each way. Verify.

## 5. Where to stay (INFERRED from general knowledge)
- **Centro Storico** (Pantheon, Navona): Best for walking and atmosphere. Cons: higher prices and tourist crowds. About 20-30 min by bus from Termini, with no metro.
- **Monti**: Central and near the Colosseum. Good restaurants and bars, and it feels local. It is a good solo base, a short walk from Cavour metro and Termini. Cons: some hills and noisy bars.
- **Trastevere**: Charming, with a lively nightlife. Cons: crowded and noisy at night, with no metro (tram 8 and buses), so it is further from the Colosseum and Vatican.
- **Prati**: Quiet, near the Vatican and Ottaviano metro, with good local restaurants and a safe feel. Cons: less atmospheric, and further from the Colosseum.
- Suggested pick for a solo first-timer: Monti, or the Centro Storico if you want to walk everywhere. This is my own opinion.
- Safety: Rome is generally safe. Pickpocketing is common at Termini, on bus 64, on metro line A and around the main sites.

## 6. Public transit (RECALLED, UNVERIFIED)
- Metro lines: A (Ottaviano for the Vatican, Spagna, Barberini, Termini), B (Colosseo, Termini, Cavour) and C (partial). Also buses and trams. Metro runs about 5:30-23:30 (to 1:30 on Fri/Sat).
- BIT single ticket €1.50, valid 100 minutes, with one metro ride. Roma Pass 24h about €7, 48h about €12.50, 72h about €18 (RECALLED, uncertain). Roma Pass (48h about €32, 72h about €52) includes museums and transit. Check these figures. Contactless bank cards were being introduced on the metro. Verify.
- Much of the centre is walkable.

## 7. Daily food costs (INFERRED estimates)
- Breakfast (cappuccino and cornetto at the bar): €2.5-4.
- Lunch (pizza al taglio, panino or a trattoria pasta): €8-15.
- Dinner (trattoria with a pasta main and wine): €20-35.
- Coperto (cover charge) €1-3 is common. Tipping is not required.
- Rough total €40-65 per day for a modest budget, or €70-100 for a sit-down lunch and dinner. This is not sourced.

Everything above. Highest-priority checks: Trevi fee status, current ticket prices, 4 Dec strike calendar, Navona market dates, Wed 2 Dec papal audience impact, Leonardo Express fare.

# Rome — 3 days, solo, Tue 1 – Fri 4 Dec 2026

**Dates:** the request said 2025, which has already passed, so this plan uses 2026.

**Flight and hotel:** both are illustrative sample data, not bookable.
- **Flight:** Meridian Air, 1 stop. Leaves BOS on Mon 30 Nov at 13:22 and takes 545 minutes. I calculated an arrival in Rome around 04:30 on 1 Dec. The search didn't return an arrival time.
- **Hotel:** Quiet guesthouse, 3 nights. The search didn't give its neighbourhood. Aim for Monti or Centro Storico.

**Book ahead:** the Borghese Gallery (reservation is mandatory), the Colosseum timed entry and the Vatican Museums timed entry.

**Daylight:** sunset is around 16:40, so do outdoor sites first.

## Day 1: Tue 1 Dec, arrival and the Centro Storico
- **Before dawn:** you land at FCO. Take the fixed-fare taxi into the centre (about €50). The Leonardo Express may not be running yet. Drop your bags at the hotel.
- **Morning:** have breakfast and coffee, then rest if your room is ready.
- **11:00:** visit the Pantheon (ticketed, about €5). Then go to Piazza Navona and have lunch nearby.
- **Afternoon:** see the Trevi Fountain (a €2 fee may apply), then the Spanish Steps.
- **15:00:** Borghese Gallery slot (2-hour visit). Afterwards, watch the sunset from the Pincio terrace.
- **Evening:** have an early dinner in Monti and an early night.

## Day 2: Wed 2 Dec, ancient Rome
Avoid the Vatican today. Wednesday is the papal audience, so St Peter's will be crowded and may have restricted access.
- **09:00:** Colosseum timed entry, then the Roman Forum and the Palatine Hill. Allow 3–4 hours.
- **Lunch:** in Monti.
- **Afternoon:** Capitoline Hill and the view over the Forum from behind the Campidoglio. Then the Circus Maximus, or the Mouth of Truth if there's no queue.
- **Evening:** cross to Trastevere for a walk and dinner.

## Day 3: Thu 3 Dec, the Vatican and Prati
- **08:30:** Vatican Museums and the Sistine Chapel, using an early timed slot.
- **Late morning:** St Peter's Basilica. You can climb the dome if you like.
- **Lunch:** in Prati.
- **Afternoon:** Castel Sant'Angelo, or walk along the Tiber and across Ponte Sant'Angelo.
- **Evening:** Campo de' Fiori, then the Jewish Ghetto for dinner. If the Piazza Navona Christmas market is open, stop there too. Its opening date is unconfirmed.

## Day 4: Fri 4 Dec, departure
- Check the strike calendar at scioperi.mit.gov.it. Fridays are common strike days.
- Take the Leonardo Express from Termini to FCO (about €14, about 32 minutes). Aim to reach the airport 3 hours before your flight. The search didn't return the return flight's departure time.
- If your flight is in the afternoon, have a last coffee and walk in the morning near the hotel.

# Rome research, 1-4 Dec 2026 (Tue-Fri), solo first-timer from Boston

## IMPORTANT LIMITATION
This session had no web search or web fetch tool, only file tools. **Nothing below was verified against a live source today (4 Nov 2026).** Everything is from my background knowledge (training data, roughly up to 2024-25) and is labelled INFERRED/RECALLED. Prices, hours and schemes may have changed. Check every item against the official sites before booking.

Failed searches (all of them, because no search tool was available): opening hours and booking rules for all attractions, Dec 2026 events and strikes, weather, FCO transfers, neighbourhoods, transit prices, food costs.

## Calendar for the trip (verified by calendar arithmetic)
- Tue 1 Dec, Wed 2 Dec, Thu 3 Dec, Fri 4 Dec 2026.
- The last Sunday of November is 29 Nov, before the trip. The free or open-Sunday Vatican day does not apply. No Sunday or Monday falls in the trip, so **the Borghese Monday closure and the Vatican Sunday closure do not affect these dates**.

## 1. Attractions (RECALLED, UNVERIFIED)
- **Colosseum / Forum / Palatine**: A combined timed ticket (the "Full Experience" and standard tickets) is sold at parcocolosseo.it. Typically open daily from about 9:00 until about 1 hour before sunset, which is around 16:30-17:00 in December. It is closed 25 Dec and 1 Jan. Tickets were about €18 for the standard combo, and prices have been rising. Names are on tickets and ID is checked. Book weeks ahead. Dec is low season, so slots are easier, but book now. Tickets are valid 24h for a one-time entry to each site.
- **Vatican Museums + Sistine Chapel**: Open Mon-Sat, about 9:00-18:00 with last entry around 16:00. Closed Sundays except the last Sunday of the month. Standard ticket about €20 plus a €5 online reservation fee. Book at tickets.museivaticani.va. Closed on religious holidays, including 8 Dec (outside the trip). I know of no closure on 1-4 Dec, but check the official calendar. Wednesday mornings (papal audience) make St Peter's Square busy, and the Basilica may be restricted. 2 Dec is a Wednesday.
- **St Peter's Basilica**: Free entry, with an optional free timed "fast track" reservation. Open about 7:00-19:00 (until about 18:30 in winter). It can close for papal ceremonies. A security queue is likely. Dress code: shoulders and knees covered. Dome climb about €8-10 by stairs or €10-15 by lift. Wednesday audience mornings can restrict access.
- **Pantheon**: Since July 2023 it has been ticketed for non-residents at about €5. Open about 9:00-19:00. Tickets are bought on site or online. Mass is held on Sat evening and Sun morning, outside the trip. Confirm the current price and booking rules.
- **Borghese Gallery**: Reservation is mandatory, with timed 2-hour slots. Open Tue-Sun, closed Monday. Ticket about €15 plus a fee, and it often sells out days ahead. Book at galleriaborghese.it. All trip days are open days, but 1 Dec is the arrival day, so Wed 2 Dec to Fri 4 Dec is better.
- **Trevi Fountain**: Free to view. In Feb 2024 the city said it would introduce a charge. In Jan 2026 I do not know the outcome. I recall a plan for a roughly €2 fee for tourists from early 2026, and I could not confirm it. **Verify.** Visit early morning or late evening to avoid crowds.
- Other first-timer picks (not researched): Spanish Steps, Piazza Navona, Campo de' Fiori, Castel Sant'Angelo, Trastevere in the evening, Capitoline Museums, Appian Way.

## 2. Holidays, events and strikes, 1-4 Dec (RECALLED, UNVERIFIED)
- No national holiday falls on 1-4 Dec. 8 Dec (Immaculate Conception) is a holiday after the trip. The Pope usually visits the Spanish Steps that day, and the area closes then.
- Christmas markets: Piazza Navona's market usually opens in early December, or sometimes on the first weekend of Dec (tends to open around 6-8 Dec and run to 6 Jan). Start dates for 2026 are unconfirmed, and it may not be open by 4 Dec. The Christmas tree and lights usually go up in early December.
- 2025-26 Jubilee has ended. Crowds should be lower than in 2025.
- Strikes (scioperi): Italy has frequent transit strikes, often on Fridays and often announced 10-15 days ahead. Check the Italian ministry's strike calendar (scioperi.mit.gov.it) for 4 Dec, which is a Friday and also your departure day. Allow extra time for the airport.

## 3. Weather and daylight (RECALLED, UNVERIFIED)
- Early December: highs about 13-14°C, lows about 5-6°C. It is wet, with about 8-10 rainy days in the month. Pack a rain jacket, layers and an umbrella.
- Sunrise about 7:15, sunset about 16:40-16:45. About 9.5 hours of daylight. Plan outdoor sites before sunset.

## 4. Airport transfer FCO to the centre (RECALLED, UNVERIFIED)
- Leonardo Express to Roma Termini: non-stop, about 32 minutes, running about every 15 minutes from about 6:23 until about 23:23. Fare was €14 (raised from €14 in 2023). Verify the fare.
- Regional train FL1 to Trastevere, Ostiense and Tiburtina: about €8, slower, cheaper.
- Fixed taxi fare from FCO to inside the Aurelian Walls: €50 (including luggage and up to 4 passengers) since 2023. Use only official white taxis. Verify.
- Shuttle buses (Terravision, SIT) at about €6-7 each way. Verify.

## 5. Where to stay (INFERRED from general knowledge)
- **Centro Storico** (Pantheon, Navona): Best for walking and atmosphere. Cons: higher prices and tourist crowds. About 20-30 min by bus from Termini, with no metro.
- **Monti**: Central and near the Colosseum. Good restaurants and bars, and it feels local. It is a good solo base, a short walk from Cavour metro and Termini. Cons: some hills and noisy bars.
- **Trastevere**: Charming, with a lively nightlife. Cons: crowded and noisy at night, with no metro (tram 8 and buses), so it is further from the Colosseum and Vatican.
- **Prati**: Quiet, near the Vatican and Ottaviano metro, with good local restaurants and a safe feel. Cons: less atmospheric, and further from the Colosseum.
- Suggested pick for a solo first-timer: Monti, or the Centro Storico if you want to walk everywhere. This is my own opinion.
- Safety: Rome is generally safe. Pickpocketing is common at Termini, on bus 64, on metro line A and around the main sites.

## 6. Public transit (RECALLED, UNVERIFIED)

# Rome — 3 days, solo, Tue 1 – Fri 4 Dec 2026

**Dates:** the request said 2025, which has already passed, so this plan uses 2026.

**Flight and hotel:** both are illustrative sample data, not bookable.
- **Flight:** Meridian Air, 1 stop. Leaves BOS on Mon 30 Nov at 13:22 and takes 545 minutes. I calculated an arrival in Rome around 04:30 on 1 Dec. The search didn't return an arrival time.
- **Hotel:** Quiet guesthouse, 3 nights. The search didn't give its neighbourhood. Aim for Monti or Centro Storico.

**Book ahead:** the Borghese Gallery (reservation is mandatory), the Colosseum timed entry and the Vatican Museums timed entry.

**Daylight:** sunset is around 16:40, so do outdoor sites first.

## Day 1: Tue 1 Dec, arrival and the Centro Storico
- **Before dawn:** you land at FCO. Take the fixed-fare taxi into the centre (about €50). The Leonardo Express may not be running yet. Drop your bags at the hotel.
- **Morning:** have breakfast and coffee, then rest if your room is ready.
- **11:00:** visit the Pantheon (ticketed, about €5). Then go to Piazza Navona and have lunch nearby.
- **Afternoon:** see the Trevi Fountain (a €2 fee may apply), then the Spanish Steps.
- **15:00:** Borghese Gallery slot (2-hour visit). Afterwards, watch the sunset from the Pincio terrace.
- **Evening:** have an early dinner in Monti and an early night.

## Day 2: Wed 2 Dec, ancient Rome
Avoid the Vatican today. Wednesday is the papal audience, so St Peter's will be crowded and may have restricted access.
- **09:00:** Colosseum timed entry, then the Roman Forum and the Palatine Hill. Allow 3–4 hours.
- **Lunch:** in Monti.
- **Afternoon:** Capitoline Hill and the view over the Forum from behind the Campidoglio. Then the Circus Maximus, or the Mouth of Truth if there's no queue.
- **Evening:** cross to Trastevere for a walk and dinner.

## Day 3: Thu 3 Dec, the Vatican and Prati
- **08:30:** Vatican Museums and the Sistine Chapel, using an early timed slot.
- **Late morning:** St Peter's Basilica. You can climb the dome if you like.
- **Lunch:** in Prati.
- **Afternoon:** Castel Sant'Angelo, or walk along the Tiber and across Ponte Sant'Angelo.
- **Evening:** Campo de' Fiori, then the Jewish Ghetto for dinner. If the Piazza Navona Christmas market is open, stop there too. Its opening date is unconfirmed.

## Day 4: Fri 4 Dec, departure
- Check the strike calendar at scioperi.mit.gov.it. Fridays are common strike days.
- Take the Leonardo Express from Termini to FCO (about €14, about 32 minutes). Aim to reach the airport 3 hours before your flight. The search didn't return the return flight's departure time.
- If your flight is in the afternoon, have a last coffee and walk in the morning near the hotel.

# Lisbon research, 10-17 May 2027 (2 adults)

## READ FIRST: sourcing status
I had no web search or browsing tool in this session. Only file tools were available. **Every search failed, and nothing below was read from a live source.** All of it is from my background knowledge, which is roughly 2024-25 vintage. Treat every price, hours entry and regulation as UNVERIFIED and re-check before booking.
Topics not verified: all 7 requested topics. These are attractions and closing days, day trips, transport and passes, food costs, weather and events, ETIAS/EES, and tourist tax.

Calendar facts (computed, reliable): 10 May 2027 is a Monday. 11 May is Tue, 16 May is Sun, and 17 May (departure) is a Monday.

## 1. Neighbourhoods and sights (recalled, unverified)
- **Alfama**: free to wander. Miradouros (Portas do Sol, Santa Luzia) are free. The Sé cathedral is free, with a paid cloister. Castelo de S. Jorge is about €15, with a resident discount. Check the closing day and whether it is open daily.
- **Baixa/Chiado**: free. The Santa Justa lift is about €6 (outside the transport pass, with a pass discount). The free alternative is the Carmo ruins side route. Arco da Rua Augusta viewing platform is paid (about €5-6).
- **Belém**: Jerónimos Monastery is about €18 and **closed Mondays**. Belém Tower is about €12 and **closed Mondays**. The MAAT and Coach Museum are paid, and the Coach Museum is also Monday-closed, as I recall. The monastery church is free. Pastéis de Belém is open daily.
  - Plan Belém for Tue-Sun. Monday 17 May is departure day, so Mondays cost you little.
  - Free admission: I recall that many national monuments are free on Sundays and holidays **for Portuguese residents only**, not tourists. I couldn't confirm this, so assume tourists pay. Under-12s are typically free.
- **Bairro Alto**: free by day. Nightlife is street drinking, and beer is about €1.50-3.
- **LX Factory**: free to walk through. There is a Sunday market. Shops and cafés are open most days.
- **Other free or cheap**: Feira da Ladra flea market (Tue and Sat). Time Out Market is touristy and pricey. Jardim da Estrela is free. Tram 28 is the cheapest sightseeing ride.
- **Free miradouros**: Graça, Senhora do Monte (best view), São Pedro de Alcântara.

## 2. Day trips (recalled, unverified)
- **Sintra**: train from Rossio is about €2.30-2.50 each way with a Viva Viagem card (card €0.50), about 40 min. Tickets from the previous year:
  - Pena Palace, about €20 for park plus palace, with a timed slot. Book online.
  - Moorish Castle, about €12.
  - Quinta da Regaleira, about €12.
  - The bus 434 loop is about €13 for a day pass. Walking is free but steep.
  - Budget one day, and pick at most 1-2 paid sights. Go on a weekday, since weekends are crowded.
- **Cascais**: train from Cais do Sodré is about €2.35-2.50 each way, 40 min. The beaches and coastal walk are free. Boca do Inferno is free.
- **Setúbal/Arrábida**: needs a train from Oriente/Entrecampos (about €4-5 each way) or a ferry/bus. Arrábida without a car is hard, and I don't know the current bus options. Treat it as optional or skip it on this budget.

## 3. Transport (recalled, unverified)
- **Airport to centre**: the metro Red Line runs from the airport to Saldanha, Alameda and Baixa-Chiado via a change. It costs about €1.85 plus the €0.50 card, so about €2.35 per person. Alternatives are the Aerobus (about €4) and the Carris buses 744 and 783 (about €2). Taxi or Uber is about €15-25.
- **Cards**: Viva Viagem/Navegante "occasional" card is €0.50. Zapping is pay-as-you-go. A Carris/Metro 24h ticket is about €7 (I'm unsure of the current price, so check). Metro single is about €1.85.
- **Tram 28**: about €3 on board, or use a pass. It is crowded and has pickpockets. Ride it early or from the terminus at Martim Moniz, or take Tram 12 instead.
- **Lisboa Card**: about €27 for 24h, about €45 for 48h and about €55 for 72h. It is probably **not worth it** on this budget, since the main free sights are free and you'd pay for only 2-3 monuments. It would pay off only if you visit Jerónimos, Belém Tower, Castelo and also take the Sintra/Cascais trains, which it may cover.

## 4. Food (recalled, estimates)
- Prato do dia at a tasca: about €8-12 per person, often with soup, drink and coffee.
- Pastel de nata: about €1.20-1.60 each. Bica (espresso) is about €0.80-1.
- Supermarket picnic (Pingo Doce, Mercadona): about €5-8 per person.
- Beer: about €1.50-2.50.
- **Budget traveller realistic**: about €25-35 per person per day, so about €50-70 per day for two. For seven days, about €350-500 for two.

## 5. May weather and events (inferred)
- Typical May highs are 21-24°C and lows 13-15°C. Some showers are possible, and Atlantic breezes make Sintra cooler and cloudier. Bring a light jacket.
- I know of no Portuguese national holiday between 10 and 17 May 2027. Lisbon's city holiday (Santo António) is 13 June, outside your dates. Sunday 16 May is Pentecost, which is not a public holiday.
- I could not check festivals, concerts or conferences for those dates. Look up the event calendar and hotel prices.

## 6. Entry requirements for US citizens (recalled, unverified)
- Portugal is in Schengen. US citizens need no visa for stays up to 90 days in any 180-day period, and a passport valid 3+ months beyond departure.
- **EES** (Entry/Exit System): I recall it began a phased rollout on 12 October 2025 and was intended to be fully operational by about April 2026. Expect fingerprint and photo registration at first entry. This may add queue time at the airport.
- **ETIAS**: I recall the EU targeting the last quarter of 2026 for launch, with a fee of €20 for ages 18-70, valid 3 years. **I could not confirm whether it is in force by May 2027.** Check the official EU site (travel-europe.europa.eu) and avoid third-party lookalike sites. If it is in force, budget about €40 for two.

## 7. Tourist tax (recalled, unverified)
- Lisbon: about €4 per person per night, for a maximum of 7 nights, ages 13+. It was €2 until 2024. For 6 nights for two, that's about €48. Check whether your accommodation collects it.

## Budget reality check (inferred)
USD 1,500 for two including JFK-LIS flights is extremely tight. May return flights alone are likely US$500-900 each, and I could not check fares. Add 6 nights of lodging (hostel or cheap guesthouse: about €25-40 per person per night), food of €350-500, transport and tourist tax, and the total will probably exceed the budget unless fares are very low. Verify fares first.

Flights/lodging are sample-data placeholders (not bookable). Opening days and prices below are unverified recollections — confirm before going.

**Mon 10 May** — Depart JFK evening (sample option: 2-stop economy, departs 19:40).
**Tue 11 May** — Arrive Lisbon (arrival time unconfirmed). Metro to centre (~€2.35 incl. card). Check in; easy walk Baixa → Praça do Comércio → Chiado. Sunset at Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara.
