# Lisbon research, 10-17 May 2027 (2 adults)

## READ FIRST: sourcing status
I had no web search or browsing tool in this session. Only file tools were available. **Every search failed, and nothing below was read from a live source.** All of it is from my background knowledge, which is roughly 2024-25 vintage. Treat every price, hours entry and regulation as UNVERIFIED and re-check before booking.
Topics not verified: all 7 requested topics. These are attractions and closing days, day trips, transport and passes, food costs, weather and events, ETIAS/EES, and tourist tax.

Calendar facts (computed, reliable): 10 May 2027 is a Monday. 11 May is Tue, 16 May is Sun, and 17 May (departure) is a Monday.

## 1. Neighbourhoods and sights (recalled, unverified)
- **Alfama**: free to wander. Miradouros (Portas do Sol, Santa Luzia) are free. The Sé cathedral is free, with a paid cloister. Castelo de S. Jorge is about €15, with a resident discount. Check the closing day and whether it is open daily.
- **Baixa/Chiado**: free. The Santa Justa lift is about €6 (outside the transport pass, with a pass discount). The free alternative is the Carmo ruins side route. Arco da Rua Augusta viewing platform is paid (about €5-6).
- **Belém**: Jerónimos Monastery is about €18 and **closed Mondays**. Belém Tower is about €12 and **closed Mondays**. The MAAT and Coach Museum are paid, and the Coach Museum is also Monday-closed, as I recall. The monastery church is free. Pastéis de Belém is open daily.
  - Plan Belém for Tue-Sun. Monday 17 May is departure day, so Mondays cost you little.
  - Free admission: I recall that many national monuments are free on Sundays and holidays **for Portuguese residents only**, not tourists. I couldn't confirm this, so assume tourists pay. Under-12s are typically free.
- **Bairro Alto**: free by day. Nightlife is street drinking, and beer is about €1.50-3.
- **LX Factory**: free to walk through. There is a Sunday market. Shops and cafés are open most days.
- **Other free or cheap**: Feira da Ladra flea market (Tue and Sat). Time Out Market is touristy and pricey. Jardim da Estrela is free. Tram 28 is the cheapest sightseeing ride.
- **Free miradouros**: Graça, Senhora do Monte (best view), São Pedro de Alcântara.

## 2. Day trips (recalled, unverified)
- **Sintra**: train from Rossio is about €2.30-2.50 each way with a Viva Viagem card (card €0.50), about 40 min. Tickets from the previous year:
  - Pena Palace, about €20 for park plus palace, with a timed slot. Book online.
  - Moorish Castle, about €12.
  - Quinta da Regaleira, about €12.
  - The bus 434 loop is about €13 for a day pass. Walking is free but steep.
  - Budget one day, and pick at most 1-2 paid sights. Go on a weekday, since weekends are crowded.
- **Cascais**: train from Cais do Sodré is about €2.35-2.50 each way, 40 min. The beaches and coastal walk are free. Boca do Inferno is free.
- **Setúbal/Arrábida**: needs a train from Oriente/Entrecampos (about €4-5 each way) or a ferry/bus. Arrábida without a car is hard, and I don't know the current bus options. Treat it as optional or skip it on this budget.

## 3. Transport (recalled, unverified)
- **Airport to centre**: the metro Red Line runs from the airport to Saldanha, Alameda and Baixa-Chiado via a change. It costs about €1.85 plus the €0.50 card, so about €2.35 per person. Alternatives are the Aerobus (about €4) and the Carris buses 744 and 783 (about €2). Taxi or Uber is about €15-25.
- **Cards**: Viva Viagem/Navegante "occasional" card is €0.50. Zapping is pay-as-you-go. A Carris/Metro 24h ticket is about €7 (I'm unsure of the current price, so check). Metro single is about €1.85.
- **Tram 28**: about €3 on board, or use a pass. It is crowded and has pickpockets. Ride it early or from the terminus at Martim Moniz, or take Tram 12 instead.
- **Lisboa Card**: about €27 for 24h, about €45 for 48h and about €55 for 72h. It is probably **not worth it** on this budget, since the main free sights are free and you'd pay for only 2-3 monuments. It would pay off only if you visit Jerónimos, Belém Tower, Castelo and also take the Sintra/Cascais trains, which it may cover.

## 4. Food (recalled, estimates)
- Prato do dia at a tasca: about €8-12 per person, often with soup, drink and coffee.
- Pastel de nata: about €1.20-1.60 each. Bica (espresso) is about €0.80-1.
- Supermarket picnic (Pingo Doce, Mercadona): about €5-8 per person.
- Beer: about €1.50-2.50.
- **Budget traveller realistic**: about €25-35 per person per day, so about €50-70 per day for two. For seven days, about €350-500 for two.

## 5. May weather and events (inferred)
- Typical May highs are 21-24°C and lows 13-15°C. Some showers are possible, and Atlantic breezes make Sintra cooler and cloudier. Bring a light jacket.
- I know of no Portuguese national holiday between 10 and 17 May 2027. Lisbon's city holiday (Santo António) is 13 June, outside your dates. Sunday 16 May is Pentecost, which is not a public holiday.
- I could not check festivals, concerts or conferences for those dates. Look up the event calendar and hotel prices.

## 6. Entry requirements for US citizens (recalled, unverified)
- Portugal is in Schengen. US citizens need no visa for stays up to 90 days in any 180-day period, and a passport valid 3+ months beyond departure.
- **EES** (Entry/Exit System): I recall it began a phased rollout on 12 October 2025 and was intended to be fully operational by about April 2026. Expect fingerprint and photo registration at first entry. This may add queue time at the airport.
- **ETIAS**: I recall the EU targeting the last quarter of 2026 for launch, with a fee of €20 for ages 18-70, valid 3 years. **I could not confirm whether it is in force by May 2027.** Check the official EU site (travel-europe.europa.eu) and avoid third-party lookalike sites. If it is in force, budget about €40 for two.

## 7. Tourist tax (recalled, unverified)
- Lisbon: about €4 per person per night, for a maximum of 7 nights, ages 13+. It was €2 until 2024. For 6 nights for two, that's about €48. Check whether your accommodation collects it.

## Budget reality check (inferred)
USD 1,500 for two including JFK-LIS flights is extremely tight. May return flights alone are likely US$500-900 each, and I could not check fares. Add 6 nights of lodging (hostel or cheap guesthouse: about €25-40 per person per night), food of €350-500, transport and tourist tax, and the total will probably exceed the budget unless fares are very low. Verify fares first.

# Trip options: LHR <-> SIN, 1 adult, business cabin

**ALL RESULTS BELOW ARE SAMPLE DATA (`source: sample-data`, `synthetic: true`). They are not live availability and are not bookable.** Both the flight search and the stay search returned this warning:
> "These are synthetic sample offers, not live availability. Prices, times, and seat/room counts are illustrative only and nothing here is bookable."

No live offers were returned, so there is no `expires_at` or `expires_in_seconds` for any result.

## Currency
The tool quoted everything in USD. The conversion to GBP uses an **assumed rate of £1 = US$1.27**. I picked this rate and the tool did not supply it. Replace it with the current rate before relying on any figure. GBP values are rounded to the nearest penny.

## Flights (round trip, 1 adult, searched with cabin=business)
`requested_cabin` was business. Every offer came back with `cabin: business`. No offer was mixed or a different cabin, and no `cabin_note` was returned.

Outbound departs LHR on 2027-03-01. Return is SIN->LHR on 2027-03-08. The search returned one fare per round trip. It gave only the outbound departure time, total duration and stops. **No return-leg times, arrival times or flight numbers were returned.** Duration is as quoted and is probably the outbound leg only. The tool does not say which leg it covers.

Arrival dates are my own calculation (London is UTC+0 and Singapore is UTC+8 in March). The tool did not return them. All four offers land on **2 March 2027** local time.

| # | Airline (sample) | Dep LHR 1 Mar | Duration | Stops | Est. arrival SIN | Cabin | Round-trip fare USD | Round-trip fare GBP (@1.27) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Blue Corridor | 12:02 | 11h28 (688 min) | 2 | ~07:30, 2 Mar | business | $1,249.25 | **£983.66** (cheapest) |
| F2 | Northwind | 15:55 | 9h38 (578 min) | 1 | ~09:33, 2 Mar | business | $1,307.82 | £1,029.78 |
| F3 | Meridian Air | 09:48 | 7h48 (468 min) | 0 | ~01:36, 2 Mar | business | $1,748.99 | £1,377.16 (fastest, nonstop) |
| F4 | Anser Airways | 18:09 | 8h33 (513 min) | 0 | ~10:42, 2 Mar | business | $1,942.19 | £1,529.28 (nonstop, arrives at a sensible hour) |

All four flights have source `sample-data` and `synthetic: true`. The warning is the one quoted above.

The sample durations are shorter than real LHR-SIN flights, which take about 13 hours or more. Treat the times and fares as illustrative only.

## Hotels (Singapore, check-in 2027-03-02, check-out 2027-03-08, **6 nights**, 1 room, 1 guest)
The check-in date comes from the 2 March arrival of all the flight candidates. Every stay is `source: sample-data`, `synthetic: true`, with the warning quoted above.

None of the results gave a neighbourhood or MRT information. The location field just says "Singapore". **I could not check whether any of them is in Marina Bay, Orchard, the CBD or Clarke Quay.** Only the names suggest anything about location.

No `due_at_accommodation` was returned for any stay. Where `free_cancellation` was absent it would mean the policy is unknown. Here it was present on every offer, either true or false.

| # | Name (sample) | Type | Rating | Nightly USD | total_cost USD | total_cost GBP (@1.27) | due_at_accommodation | Free cancellation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | Budget hostel, private room | hostel | 7.8 | $152.11 | $912.66 | **£718.63** (cheapest) | none returned | false |
| H2 | Quiet guesthouse | guesthouse | 9.1 | $192.37 | $1,154.22 | £908.84 | none returned | true |
| H3 | Business district hotel | hotel | 8.2 | $230.63 | $1,383.78 | £1,089.59 | none returned | false |
| H4 | Central boutique hotel | hotel | 8.9 | $301.15 | $1,806.90 | £1,422.76 | none returned | false |

A fifth result, "Riverside apartment" (apartment, rating 8.6, $264.89 a night, $1,589.34 total, about £1,251.45, free cancellation true), was also returned. I left it out of the table to keep to four.

## Budget check (£9,000 for flights + hotel)
Every combination is far under budget.
- **Cheapest:** F1 + H1 = £983.66 + £718.63 = **£1,702.29**.
- **Most convenient:** F3 (nonstop, earliest departure) or F4 (nonstop, civilised arrival) with H3 or H4. F3 + H4 is £1,377.16 + £1,422.76 = **£2,799.92**. F4 + H3 is £1,529.28 + £1,089.59 = £2,618.87.
- The most expensive pairing, F4 + H4, is £1,529.28 + £1,422.76 = £2,952.04.

## Cheapest vs most convenient
- **Cheapest:** F1 (Blue Corridor) with H1 (hostel) comes to about £1,702. F1 has 2 stops. The sample duration is about 11.5 hours, which is longer than the nonstops. H1 is a hostel private room with a 7.8 rating and no free cancellation. Its central location is unverified.
- **Most convenient:** F3 or F4 is nonstop. F3 saves about 45 minutes, but its estimated arrival is around 01:36, which is awkward for a 2 March check-in. F4 leaves at 18:09 and lands mid-morning, so an early check-in would be needed. A central-sounding hotel (H3 or H4) adds roughly £370 to £700 over the hostel.
- **Tradeoff:** going nonstop costs about £390 to £545 more than F1 and saves 1 to 2 stops. That is minor against the £9,000 budget. Both searches returned sample data, so none of these rankings is a real availability or price comparison.

## Sample vs live
- **Sample data:** F1, F2, F3, F4, H1, H2, H3, H4, and the fifth stay (Riverside apartment).
- **Live:** none.
- Flights and stays both came from `sample-data` and were checked separately.

## Gaps to fix before any booking
- Re-run both searches against live inventory.
- Get the return-leg times and the actual arrival times.
- Confirm hotel neighbourhoods and MRT access.
- Replace the assumed GBP rate with a current one.

- Neighbourhoods [UNVERIFIED-MEMORY/INFERRED]:
  - The historic canal ring (Jordaan, Grachtengordel, the Negen Straatjes) has cobbles, narrow pavements, bridges with humps, and many hotels with steps or tiny lifts. It is the harder option.
  - Flatter, newer areas are generally easier: Museumkwartier/Oud-Zuid (near the Rijksmuseum, Van Gogh Museum and Stedelijk, with smoother brick or asphalt in places), Amsterdam Oost near Artis, the Eastern Docklands/Oosterdok around Centraal, and the Zuidas business district. Chain hotels near Centraal, Oosterdok and Museumplein often have lifts and adapted rooms.

## Day 3 — Wed 4 Aug: Water & Noord
- Late morning: wheelchair-accessible canal cruise. Book a boat with a lift or ramp and confirm it in advance. Specific operators are UNCONFIRMED.
- Afternoon: free ferry from behind Centraal to Noord (believed step-free roll-on, UNCONFIRMED), then A'DAM Lookout. The lift to the deck is believed to exist; check access to the outdoor deck and swing.
- Dinner in Noord or around Centraal.

## Day 4 — Thu 5 Aug: Plantage & Oosterdok
- Morning: Hortus Botanicus. Some greenhouses may have steps or narrow paths (UNCONFIRMED).
- Afternoon: NEMO Science Museum. Lifts are believed available; the rooftop terrace is reached by a sloped approach (UNCONFIRMED).
- Anne Frank House: the original house has steep stairs. Wheelchair access is limited or partial (UNCONFIRMED). If you want to go, book the timed ticket weeks ahead and ask about access.
- Note: Pride week is likely under way. The Canal Parade is expected on Sat 7 Aug, after you leave (date UNCONFIRMED). Expect crowds and possible closures in the centre.

## Day 5 — Fri 6 Aug: Depart
- Relaxed morning: Museumplein or a café.
- Wheelchair taxi to Schiphol, arriving at least 2.5 h before departure. Check in for PRM assistance.

## Confirm before booking
Hotel accessibility (step-free entrance, lift, roll-in shower) · PRM assistance with the airline · step-free GVB tram stops and the NS boarding ramp · accessible canal cruise operator · museum and attraction access details, opening hours and prices for early August · step-free vegetarian restaurants with accessible toilets · Pride 2027 dates and closures · wheelchair-taxi firms and fares.

# Amsterdam research, 2027-08-02 to 2027-08-06 (wheelchair user, vegetarian, solo, from Dublin)

## IMPORTANT: verification status
My tools in this session were file tools only (ls, read, write, grep, glob). I had no web search or browsing tool. **Nothing below was read from a source today.** Every item is background knowledge from my training data or an inference, and it may be out of date. Prices, hours and schedules must be checked on official sites before booking.

Labels: [UNVERIFIED-MEMORY] means recalled from training and not checked. [INFERRED] means reasoned from general patterns. [NOT CHECKED] means I have no information.

## 1. Wheelchair accessibility
- Neighbourhoods [UNVERIFIED-MEMORY/INFERRED]:
  - The historic canal ring (Jordaan, Grachtengordel, the Negen Straatjes) has cobbles, narrow pavements, bridges with humps, and many hotels with steps or tiny lifts. It is the harder option.
  - Flatter, newer areas are generally easier: Museumkwartier/Oud-Zuid (near the Rijksmuseum, Van Gogh Museum and Stedelijk, with smoother brick or asphalt in places), Amsterdam Oost near Artis, the Eastern Docklands/Oosterdok around Centraal, and the Zuidas business district. Chain hotels near Centraal, Oosterdok and Museumplein often have lifts and adapted rooms.
  - Choose a hotel by confirming a step-free entrance, lift dimensions and a roll-in shower directly with the hotel. [NOT CHECKED: no specific hotels researched]
- GVB trams, bus and metro [UNVERIFIED-MEMORY]:
  - Most of the current tram fleet is low-floor with a ramp that the driver deploys. Boarding is generally fine, but I did not verify which lines or stops are step-free. Check the GVB accessibility pages and the 9292 journey planner.
  - Metro lines have lifts at most stations. Lifts can be out of service, so check live status.
  - The GVB ferries behind Centraal to Noord are free and step-free in general. Not verified.
- Taxis [NOT CHECKED]: I did not research wheelchair-adapted taxi firms or fares. The Netherlands has adapted taxi and "Valys" schemes, but Valys is for Dutch residents. Ask the hotel or pre-book an adapted taxi or transfer.
- Schiphol to the city [UNVERIFIED-MEMORY]:
  - Trains from Schiphol Plaza station to Amsterdam Centraal take about 15-20 minutes and run very frequently. The station has lifts, and NS offers a boarding ramp with staff.
  - NS assistance usually needs booking, at least 1 hour in advance for the same day. Check the NS "Reisassistentie" page for the current rule and phone number.
  - Dublin departure: ask the airline or Dublin Airport for PRM assistance at least 48 hours ahead. Schiphol's PRM service is arranged through the airline. [NOT CHECKED: current procedure]

## 2. Attractions
I did not verify any hours, ticket prices or access details. The notes are recalled and may be out of date.
- Rijksmuseum: generally well accessible, with a step-free entrance and lifts. Typically open daily. Adult ticket was roughly €22.50-€25 [UNVERIFIED-MEMORY]. Book timed slots online.
- Van Gogh Museum: accessible with lifts. Timed tickets are required. Adult ticket was about €22-€25. Typically open daily.
- Stedelijk: accessible, with a step-free new-wing entrance. Adult ticket was about €21-€22.
- NEMO: accessible and has lifts. Adult ticket was about €20-€22. Open daily in school holidays. The building is a ship-shaped landmark with a long slope or stairs, so check the step-free route.
- Hermitage / H'ART Museum: Hermitage Amsterdam was renamed H'ART. I do not know the current programme, access or price. [NOT CHECKED]
- Anne Frank House: the historic building has steep stairs and is **not** step-free in the original part. A new-building wheelchair route is said to exist, but I did not check it. Tickets are timed, online only, and sell out weeks ahead. Price was about €16-€17. [UNVERIFIED-MEMORY, high priority to check]
- Canal cruises: some operators have boats with a ramp or a low entry, but I did not verify which. Ask for a wheelchair-accessible boat when booking.
- Vondelpark: flat paths, free entry. [INFERRED]
- A'DAM Lookout: the building has lifts. The swing and other features may not be accessible. [NOT CHECKED]
- Artis: mostly flat paths, but I did not verify details or price. [NOT CHECKED]
- Hortus Botanicus: has some historic paths with gravel and steps. [NOT CHECKED]
- Zaanse Schans: flat in parts, but with gravel and wooden mills with steps. Reachable by train to Koog-Zaandijk plus a walk or a bus. [NOT CHECKED]

## 3. Vegetarian and vegan restaurants
[NOT CHECKED: I verified no restaurant for step-free access, accessible toilets or price.] Amsterdam has a strong vegetarian scene, and a typical main costs about €15-€25 [INFERRED]. Specific names must be researched and then confirmed by phone or email for access.

## 4. Early August
- Weather [INFERRED]: typical highs are about 21-23°C, with showers likely, so pack a rain layer.
- Crowds: peak summer, so book museums and the Anne Frank House early.
- Pride: Amsterdam Pride usually runs from late July into the first week of August, with the Canal Parade on the first Saturday of August. For 2027 that would likely be **Saturday 7 August 2027**, one day after the trip ends, but I did not confirm it. Pride-week events and street closures could overlap the stay. [INFERRED, NOT CHECKED]
- Closures: not checked.

## 5. Costs
[NOT CHECKED against current prices.] Rough planning figures from memory, all unverified:
- GVB day tickets cost about €9-€10 for 1 day, with multi-day passes also on sale. Verify.
- Food: about €40-€70 per day.
- Contactless OV-payment (tap in with a bank card) is possible on GVB. Verify.

## Failed or skipped topics (all of them, because no search tool was available)

# Amsterdam — Mon 2 Aug to Fri 6 Aug 2027 (4 nights)
Solo traveler · wheelchair user · vegetarian · budget €2500 (est. €2110)

**Base:** Museumplein-area modern hotel (sample "business district hotel"). Museum Quarter is flat with wide pavements. Before booking, confirm directly with the hotel: step-free entrance, lift, accessible room with roll-in shower.
**Flights:** Nonstop return, economy (sample-data, not bookable). Book PRM wheelchair assistance with the airline at booking or at least 48 h ahead. Declare the chair type and battery.
**Getting around:** GVB low-floor trams plus wheelchair taxis. Which tram stops are step-free is UNCONFIRMED. Check the GVB accessibility map before travelling.
**Pacing:** One main area per day, with rest time in the afternoons.

## Day 1 — Mon 2 Aug: Arrive
- Morning nonstop from DUB, with PRM assistance at both airports.
- Pre-booked wheelchair taxi from Schiphol to the hotel. Alternative: NS train to Centraal (lifts and boarding ramp believed available; ramp may need booking ahead; UNCONFIRMED).
- Afternoon: easy roll in Vondelpark on its flat paved paths.
- Dinner: a vegetarian restaurant near the hotel. Check step-free entry and an accessible toilet when booking.

## Day 2 — Tue 3 Aug: Museumplein
- Rijksmuseum in the morning (timed ticket).
- Lunch at the museum café.
- Afternoon: Van Gogh Museum (timed ticket, book ahead). Step-free access and wheelchair loans are believed available at both museums but are UNCONFIRMED.
- Optional: Stedelijk, next door.

## Day 3 — Wed 4 Aug: Water & Noord
- Late morning: wheelchair-accessible canal cruise. Book a boat with a lift or ramp and confirm it in advance. Specific operators are UNCONFIRMED.
- Afternoon: free ferry from behind Centraal to Noord (believed step-free roll-on, UNCONFIRMED), then A'DAM Lookout. The lift to the deck is believed to exist; check access to the outdoor deck and swing.
- Dinner in Noord or around Centraal.

## Day 4 — Thu 5 Aug: Plantage & Oosterdok
- Morning: Hortus Botanicus. Some greenhouses may have steps or narrow paths (UNCONFIRMED).
- Afternoon: NEMO Science Museum. Lifts are believed available; the rooftop terrace is reached by a sloped approach (UNCONFIRMED).
- Anne Frank House: the original house has steep stairs. Wheelchair access is limited or partial (UNCONFIRMED). If you want to go, book the timed ticket weeks ahead and ask about access.
- Note: Pride week is likely under way. The Canal Parade is expected on Sat 7 Aug, after you leave (date UNCONFIRMED). Expect crowds and possible closures in the centre.

## Day 5 — Fri 6 Aug: Depart
- Relaxed morning: Museumplein or a café.
- Wheelchair taxi to Schiphol, arriving at least 2.5 h before departure. Check in for PRM assistance.

## Confirm before booking
Hotel accessibility (step-free entrance, lift, roll-in shower) · PRM assistance with the airline · step-free GVB tram stops and the NS boarding ramp · accessible canal cruise operator · museum and attraction access details, opening hours and prices for early August · step-free vegetarian restaurants with accessible toilets · Pride 2027 dates and closures · wheelchair-taxi firms and fares.

# Tokyo research, 8-15 Nov 2027 (Mon to Mon, 7 nights)

## IMPORTANT: sourcing status
My tools in this session were file tools only. I had no web search or fetch. **Nothing below was read from a source or verified.** All of it is background knowledge, and some is inference. It may be stale. Every item needs a check before booking.

Failed topics (all of them, because no search was possible): neighbourhoods, attractions and opening days, foliage timing, day trips, transit fares and airport transfers, daily costs, holidays and events, entry requirements and JESTA.

Date check (calculated): 8 Nov 2027 is a Monday and 15 Nov 2027 is a Monday.

## Read from a source
None.

## Inferred or recalled, unverified

### Entry (check first)
- US passport holders have historically been visa-exempt for tourism of up to 90 days. The passport must be valid for the stay.
- Visit Japan Web (online immigration and customs pre-registration) is optional but speeds arrival.
- JESTA is a proposed US-ESTA-style pre-travel authorisation. I recall it was announced but not live, with a launch expected around 2028. I do not know whether it will be in force by Nov 2027. **Check the Japanese MOFA and immigration sites before travel.**

### Base neighbourhood (my recommendation: Shinjuku, or Tokyo Station/Ginza as the alternative)
- **Shinjuku**
  - Pros: big rail hub, direct Narita Express, Haneda limousine buses, easy Hakone (Odakyu Romancecar) and Kawagoe access, lots of food, nightlife.
  - Cons: the station is a maze, the area is busy and loud, and Kabukicho is gaudy.
- **Shibuya**
  - Pros: young, trendy, close to Harajuku and Meiji Shrine.
  - Cons: hilly, crowded, fewer mid-range hotels.
- **Tokyo Station/Ginza**
  - Pros: Shinkansen and Narita Express, calm, upmarket, central.
  - Cons: pricier, quieter at night.
- **Asakusa/Ueno**
  - Pros: cheaper, traditional feel, Skyliner to Narita at Ueno, near museums.
  - Cons: farther from west Tokyo, and Asakusa goes quiet early.
- Suggested: Shinjuku for first-timers. Choose Tokyo Station if the plan is heavy on day trips by Shinkansen.

### Attractions and closures (recall; verify)
- Monday closures:
  - Tokyo National Museum, Ueno: closed Mondays.
  - Nezu Museum: closed Mondays.
  - Shinjuku Gyoen: closed Mondays.
  - Imperial Palace East Gardens: closed Mondays and Fridays.
  - Many museums are closed on Mondays. Check each one.
- Mostly daily:
  - Senso-ji grounds.
  - Meiji Shrine.
  - teamLab Planets and Borderless (book ahead).
- Ghibli Museum: closed Tuesdays, and tickets must be bought in advance.
- Tsukiji Outer Market: many stalls close Sundays and some Wednesdays.
- Toyosu: closed on set market holidays.
- The Edo-Tokyo Museum was closed for renovation. I am not sure of its reopening status.
- Plan the Monday of 8 Nov (arrival day) and 15 Nov (departure day) around the closures. Put shrines, neighbourhood walks and Shibuya Sky on the Monday.

### Foliage (inferred from typical timing; shifts year to year)
- Tokyo (ginkgo, maple, Meiji Jingu Gaien, Rikugien, Koishikawa Korakuen): usually peaks late Nov to early Dec. Mid-Nov is likely early or partial colour.
- Nikko: peaks mid-Oct to early Nov, so likely past peak by 8-15 Nov. Lower areas such as Toshogu may still have colour.
- Hakone: peaks roughly mid to late Nov, so a good bet for this window.
- Kamakura: peaks late Nov to early Dec, so probably early.
- Check the Japan Meteorological Corporation or Japan Guide foliage forecast, which is usually published from September.

### Day trips
- Hakone, 2 hours from Shinjuku by Odakyu. Check the Hakone Free Pass.
- Kamakura, about 1 hour.
- Nikko, about 2 hours.
- Kawagoe.
- Yokohama.
- Mt Fuji and Kawaguchiko.
- Suggestion for a week: Hakone plus one of Kamakura or Nikko.

### Transit
- **Suica/PASMO**
  - Mobile Suica works on iPhone Apple Wallet.
  - The physical card supply has been restricted. Welcome Suica is a tourist version, and I am unsure of its current availability.
  - Fares are about ¥150-300 per ride in the city.
- **Narita to central Tokyo** (approximate, from memory)
  - Narita Express (N'EX): about ¥3,000+, 60-90 minutes.
  - Keisei Skyliner to Ueno: about ¥2,500, 40 minutes.
  - Limousine bus: about ¥3,000.
  - Cheaper rail: about ¥1,000-1,300.
- **Haneda**
  - Keikyu or Monorail: about ¥300-500.
  - Limousine bus: about ¥1,300-1,600.
  - Taxi: about ¥6,000-10,000.
- Fares may have risen since.

### Holidays and events
- Nov 15 is Shichi-Go-San (children aged 3, 5 and 7 in kimono at shrines). It is not a public holiday, and families visit on the nearest weekends.
- Culture Day (Nov 3) and Labour Thanksgiving (Nov 23) both fall outside the window.
- Tori-no-ichi (Asakusa Otori Shrine) falls in November on Rooster days. I did not calculate the 2027 dates. Check them.
- Weather: expect about 10-18°C, mostly dry, with cool evenings.

### Costs, mid-range for 2 (USD, rough estimate at ~¥150/$; unverified)
- Hotel: $150-250 per night.
- Food: $90-140 per day.
- Local transit: $10-20 per day.
- Activities: $20-60 per day.
- Total excluding hotel: about $130-220 per day. Including hotel: about $280-470 per day.
- Add one day-trip for $60-150.

I wrote the candidates to `/trip/options.md`. Every result came back as `source: sample-data`, and none of it is live or bookable. Each search carried the warning "synthetic sample offers, not live availability… nothing here is bookable." Treat all prices as illustrative planning figures.

None of the offers had `expires_at` or `due_at_accommodation`, and none reported a bed type. Whether any room has a double or queen bed is unverified. Every offer stated its cancellation terms, so none were missing.

I searched Tokyo generally, plus Shinjuku, Shibuya, Ginza and Ueno. I did not search Asakusa separately.

**Cheapest (all sample-data)**
- **Ginza Quiet guesthouse:** $120.39 a night, $842.73 total, free cancellation, rated 9.1. Its refundable terms make it the best low-cost pick.
- **Ginza Business district hotel:** $145.61 a night, $1,019.27 total, non-refundable, rated 8.2. It is the cheaper hotel-style option.
- **Ginza Budget hostel private room:** $97.17 a night, $680.19 total, non-refundable, rated 7.8. It is the absolute cheapest, but I don't recommend it.

**Mid (all sample-data)**
- **Ginza Riverside apartment:** $167.83 a night, $1,174.81 total, free cancellation, rated 8.6.
- **Shinjuku Business district hotel:** $248.16 a night, $1,737.12 total, free cancellation, rated 8.2. This is the choice if you want to be in Shinjuku.

**Nicer (all sample-data)**
- **Ginza Central boutique hotel:** $190.05 a night, $1,330.35 total, non-refundable, rated 8.9.
- **Central boutique hotel, Tokyo (area unspecified):** $290 a night, $2,030 total, free cancellation, rated 8.9.

**Cheapest vs. most convenient**
- **Ginza is cheapest and well placed.** It is next to Tokyo Station and has the lowest prices in this data, from $120 to $190 a night. The 7-night totals run from about $0.8k to $1.3k, which leaves most of the ~$6,000 budget for flights.
- **Shinjuku costs more.** It is the best-connected area for rail and nightlife, at about $168 to $288 a night. The Business hotel there is about $100 a night more than the Ginza equivalent, roughly $720 more over the stay.
- **Ueno and Shibuya were pricier.** Ueno had only a hostel and a guesthouse, at $209 to $258 a night. Shibuya was $193 to $288.
- **Cancellation terms differ.** The cheapest hotel-style and nicer Ginza options are non-refundable, while the refundable ones cost a little more.
- **The area pricing is a data artifact.** The sample data scales prices by area, so Ginza looks unusually cheap. Re-run the searches against live inventory before relying on any area comparison.

They may be out of date, and the file says so. The topics I couldn't check are neighbourhoods, attractions and opening days, foliage timing, day trips, transit fares and airport transfers, daily costs, holidays and events, and entry requirements including JESTA.

What most affects the plan:

1. **Entry.** US passport holders have historically been visa-exempt for up to 90 days. JESTA is a proposed pre-travel authorisation, and I recall it launching around 2028. I don't know whether it will be in force by November 2027, so check the Japanese immigration and foreign ministry sites.
2. **Base.** I suggest Shinjuku for a first visit. It has direct rail and bus links from Narita and Haneda, an easy route to Hakone, and plenty of food and nightlife. Tokyo Station/Ginza is the alternative if you plan several Shinkansen day trips.
3. **Monday closures.** Both 8 and 15 Nov are Mondays. From memory, these places are closed on Mondays:
   - Tokyo National Museum
   - Nezu Museum
   - Shinjuku Gyoen
   - Imperial Palace East Gardens (also closed Fridays)

   Put shrines and neighbourhood walks on those days. The Ghibli Museum is closed Tuesdays and needs advance tickets.
4. **Foliage, inferred from typical timing.**
   - Hakone should be near peak in mid-November.
   - Nikko is probably past peak.
   - Tokyo and Kamakura are likely only partly coloured, because they usually peak from late November to early December.
   - Choose Hakone as the main day trip, then check the foliage forecasts closer to the date.
5. **Cost estimate, unverified.** I assumed about ¥150 to the dollar.
   - Excluding the hotel, about $130–220 per day for two people: food $90–140, local transit $10–20, activities $20–60.
   - Hotel at mid-range, $150–250 per night.
   - Total about $280–470 per day.
   - A day trip adds about $60–150.

Nov 15 is Shichi-Go-San, when children dress in kimono for shrine visits. It isn't a public holiday. I didn't work out the 2027 dates for the Tori-no-ichi festival at Asakusa, so check those.

I also couldn't confirm the Narita and Haneda transfer prices. From memory, rail from Haneda costs about ¥300–500 and the Narita Express about ¥3,000. Fares may have risen since.

# Tokyo research, 8-15 Nov 2027 (Mon to Mon, 7 nights)

## IMPORTANT: sourcing status
My tools in this session were file tools only. I had no web search or fetch. **Nothing below was read from a source or verified.** All of it is background knowledge, and some is inference. It may be stale. Every item needs a check before booking.

Failed topics (all of them, because no search was possible): neighbourhoods, attractions and opening days, foliage timing, day trips, transit fares and airport transfers, daily costs, holidays and events, entry requirements and JESTA.

Date check (calculated): 8 Nov 2027 is a Monday and 15 Nov 2027 is a Monday.

## Read from a source
None.

## Inferred or recalled, unverified

### Entry (check first)
- US passport holders have historically been visa-exempt for tourism of up to 90 days. The passport must be valid for the stay.
- Visit Japan Web (online immigration and customs pre-registration) is optional but speeds arrival.
- JESTA is a proposed US-ESTA-style pre-travel authorisation. I recall it was announced but not live, with a launch expected around 2028. I do not know whether it will be in force by Nov 2027. **Check the Japanese MOFA and immigration sites before travel.**

### Base neighbourhood (my recommendation: Shinjuku, or Tokyo Station/Ginza as the alternative)
- **Shinjuku**
  - Pros: big rail hub, direct Narita Express, Haneda limousine buses, easy Hakone (Odakyu Romancecar) and Kawagoe access, lots of food, nightlife.
  - Cons: the station is a maze, the area is busy and loud, and Kabukicho is gaudy.
- **Shibuya**
  - Pros: young, trendy, close to Harajuku and Meiji Shrine.
  - Cons: hilly, crowded, fewer mid-range hotels.
- **Tokyo Station/Ginza**
  - Pros: Shinkansen and Narita Express, calm, upmarket, central.
  - Cons: pricier, quieter at night.
- **Asakusa/Ueno**
  - Pros: cheaper, traditional feel, Skyliner to Narita at Ueno, near museums.
  - Cons: farther from west Tokyo, and Asakusa goes quiet early.
- Suggested: Shinjuku for first-timers. Choose Tokyo Station if the plan is heavy on day trips by Shinkansen.

### Attractions and closures (recall; verify)
- Monday closures:
  - Tokyo National Museum, Ueno: closed Mondays.
  - Nezu Museum: closed Mondays.
  - Shinjuku Gyoen: closed Mondays.
  - Imperial Palace East Gardens: closed Mondays and Fridays.
  - Many museums are closed on Mondays. Check each one.
- Mostly daily:
  - Senso-ji grounds.
  - Meiji Shrine.
  - teamLab Planets and Borderless (book ahead).
- Ghibli Museum: closed Tuesdays, and tickets must be bought in advance.
- Tsukiji Outer Market: many stalls close Sundays and some Wednesdays.
- Toyosu: closed on set market holidays.
- The Edo-Tokyo Museum was closed for renovation. I am not sure of its reopening status.
- Plan the Monday of 8 Nov (arrival day) and 15 Nov (departure day) around the closures. Put shrines, neighbourhood walks and Shibuya Sky on the Monday.

### Foliage (inferred from typical timing; shifts year to year)
- Tokyo (ginkgo, maple, Meiji Jingu Gaien, Rikugien, Koishikawa Korakuen): usually peaks late Nov to early Dec. Mid-Nov is likely early or partial colour.
- Nikko: peaks mid-Oct to early Nov, so likely past peak by 8-15 Nov. Lower areas such as Toshogu may still have colour.
- Hakone: peaks roughly mid to late Nov, so a good bet for this window.
- Kamakura: peaks late Nov to early Dec, so probably early.
- Check the Japan Meteorological Corporation or Japan Guide foliage forecast, which is usually published from September.

### Day trips
- Hakone, 2 hours from Shinjuku by Odakyu. Check the Hakone Free Pass.
- Kamakura, about 1 hour.
- Nikko, about 2 hours.
- Kawagoe.
- Yokohama.
- Mt Fuji and Kawaguchiko.
- Suggestion for a week: Hakone plus one of Kamakura or Nikko.

### Transit
- **Suica/PASMO**
  - Mobile Suica works on iPhone Apple Wallet.
  - The physical card supply has been restricted. Welcome Suica is a tourist version, and I am unsure of its current availability.
  - Fares are about ¥150-300 per ride in the city.
- **Narita to central Tokyo** (approximate, from memory)
  - Narita Express (N'EX): about ¥3,000+, 60-90 minutes.
  - Keisei Skyliner to Ueno: about ¥2,500, 40 minutes.
  - Limousine bus: about ¥3,000.
  - Cheaper rail: about ¥1,000-1,300.
- **Haneda**
  - Keikyu or Monorail: about ¥300-500.
  - Limousine bus: about ¥1,300-1,600.
  - Taxi: about ¥6,000-10,000.
- Fares may have risen since.

### Holidays and events
- Nov 15 is Shichi-Go-San (children aged 3, 5 and 7 in kimono at shrines). It is not a public holiday, and families visit on the nearest weekends.
- Culture Day (Nov 3) and Labour Thanksgiving (Nov 23) both fall outside the window.
- Tori-no-ichi (Asakusa Otori Shrine) falls in November on Rooster days. I did not calculate the 2027 dates. Check them.
- Weather: expect about 10-18°C, mostly dry, with cool evenings.

### Costs, mid-range for 2 (USD, rough estimate at ~¥150/$; unverified)
- Hotel: $150-250 per night.
- Food: $90-140 per day.
- Local transit: $10-20 per day.
- Activities: $20-60 per day.
- Total excluding hotel: about $130-220 per day. Including hotel: about $280-470 per day.
- Add one day-trip for $60-150.

Opening days below are from unverified background knowledge — confirm before going.

**Mon 8 Nov — Arrive.** Transfer from Narita (Narita Express/Skyliner) or Haneda (Keikyu/monorail). Get Suica cards. Evening stroll in Ginza, dinner in the Yurakucho izakaya alleys under the train tracks. (Many museums are closed on Mondays, so the day is kept light.)

**Tue 9 Nov — Old Tokyo.** Morning at Senso-ji and Nakamise in Asakusa. Afternoon in Ueno Park and the Tokyo National Museum (believed closed Mondays, so Tuesday). Late-afternoon walk around Yanaka. Check whether the Tori-no-ichi festival at Asakusa falls this week (2027 dates unchecked).

**Wed 10 Nov — West side.** Meiji Jingu, then Harajuku and Omotesando, Nezu Museum (believed closed Mondays). Evening at Shibuya Crossing and the Shibuya Sky viewpoint (book a sunset slot).

**Thu 11 Nov — Hakone day trip.** Romancecar from Shinjuku, then the Hakone loop: Tozan railway, ropeway past Owakudani, Lake Ashi boat. Mid-November is typically near peak foliage here (inferred; check the forecast nearer the date). Leave Tokyo early.

**Fri 12 Nov — Markets & bay.** Breakfast at Tsukiji Outer Market, then Hama-rikyu Gardens. Afternoon at teamLab (Planets or Borderless; book ahead) and Odaiba. Note: Imperial Palace East Gardens are believed closed on Fridays, so they go on Sunday.

**Sat 13 Nov — Shinjuku.** Shinjuku Gyoen gardens (autumn colour starting), free views from the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building, evening in Omoide Yokocho and Golden Gai.

**Sun 14 Nov — Flex day.** Imperial Palace East Gardens in the morning. Then pick one: Kamakura day trip (likely only partly coloured), the Ghibli Museum in Mitaka plus Kichijoji (tickets sell out early), or Akihabara and Yanaka shopping. Farewell dinner.

**Mon 15 Nov — Depart.** It is Shichi-Go-San, so if time allows, look for families in kimono at Meiji Jingu or another shrine. Then the airport transfer.

## Confirm before booking
- Entry rules for your passport, including whether the JESTA pre-arrival authorisation is in force by Nov 2027 (unchecked)
- Museum and garden closing days (unchecked)
- Airport rail fares (unchecked)
- Foliage forecasts
- 2027 Tori-no-ichi dates
- Real hotel availability and price (only sample data so far)

# Paris (2027-09-04 to 09-08) and Rome (2027-09-08 to 09-13): research notes

## READ THIS FIRST: provenance
- **No web search or browsing tool was available in this session.** I only had file tools. Nothing below was verified against a live source.
- Everything is **from my background knowledge (training data), not read on a source today (2026-11-04)**. Prices and rules are probably 1-3 years old and may have changed by Sept 2027.
- Every figure is an estimate to re-check on the official site before booking.
- Failed or not done, every topic: all web searches. Topics that needed searching: current ticket prices, 2027 events and closures, ETIAS/EES status, Paris and Rome transit fares, taxi and transfer fares, train and flight prices, tourist tax rates, weather. None of these were confirmed.

## Entry requirements (US passport), unverified
- Schengen area: France and Italy both. 90 days in 180 without a visa. Passport should be valid 3+ months beyond departure. Ideally have 6 months.
- **EES (Entry/Exit System)**: biometric registration at the border. Its launch was scheduled for 12 Oct 2025 with a phased rollout over about 6 months. Under that plan it should be live by Sept 2027. **Not confirmed.** Expect fingerprint and photo at first entry, and possible queues.
- **ETIAS**: about €7 online authorisation for visa-exempt travelers. It was expected to start in the last quarter of 2026. Delays are common. **Whether it will be required by Sept 2027 is unconfirmed.** Check travel-europe.europa.eu/etias and the US State Department pages about 3 months before departure. Use official sites only, because look-alike scam sites exist.

## Paris

### Where to stay (inference from general knowledge)
- **Le Marais (3rd/4th)**: central, walkable, lively, good food. Metro lines 1, 11, 8, 9.
- **Saint-Germain-des-Prés / Latin Quarter (5th/6th)**: classic, safe, restaurants. Metro 4, 10, 12. RER B at Saint-Michel and Luxembourg.
- **Île Saint-Louis / Louvre-Tuileries (1st)**: central, pricier.
- **Avoid for a solo first visit**: areas around Gare du Nord, Gare de l'Est, Barbès and Pigalle at night. They are fine for transit but can feel rough late. Pickpockets are common at the Eiffel Tower, Louvre, Metro line 1 and Montmartre.
- Mid-range hotel rate guess: €150-250 per night in September. Sept is busy (rentrée, trade fairs), so book early.

### Attractions: prices and closures (from memory, verify)
| Sight | Approx. price | Closed | Booking |
|---|---|---|---|
| Louvre | €22 (rose to about €22 in 2024; a non-EU surcharge was discussed for 2026, unconfirmed) | **Tuesday** | Timed slot required, book ahead |
| Eiffel Tower | Lift to summit about €36-40, stairs to 2nd floor about €13-15 | Open daily | Book weeks ahead. Tickets release about 60 days out |
| Sainte-Chapelle | About €13-15 | Open daily | Timed slot recommended |
| Musée d'Orsay | About €16-18 | **Monday** | Book ahead |
| Notre-Dame (cathedral) | Free | Open daily | Reopened Dec 2024. Optional free reservation to skip the queue |
| Versailles (if added) | Palace about €21-32 | **Monday** | Timed ticket. Château closes Mondays |
| Arc de Triomphe top | About €16 | Open daily | Book ahead |
- The Musée d'Orsay and Louvre may have ticket rules or hours that have changed. Check the official sites.
- Sunday free-entry rules (e.g. first Sunday of the month at some museums) have been changing. Unconfirmed.

### Transfers and transit (from memory)
- **CDG to centre**:
  - RER B: about €13-14, 35-50 min. The fare rose in 2024-25. Verify.
  - Taxi flat rate: about €56 (Right Bank) or €65 (Left Bank).
  - Roissybus: about €16-17.
  - Late arrival: RER B has security issues at night, and works sometimes cut service.
- **Transit**:
  - Single Metro ticket: about €2.50. The price rose in 2025 to about €2.50 (€2.55 on cards).
  - Navigo Easy card: about €2 for the card. Carnets of 10 are cheaper per ride.
  - **Navigo Decouverte weekly**: about €32 and valid **Monday to Sunday only**. Poor value for a Saturday to Wednesday stay.
  - Paris Visite pass: pricier. Likely worse than individual tickets for a moderate-pace stay.
  - Most sights are within walkable or 1-2 Metro-ride range, so budget about €10-15 total on rides.
- **Taxe de séjour**: charged by the hotel per person per night. For 3-4 star hotels roughly €3-5 per night, including the regional surcharge. The 2025 rise was reported but not confirmed.

### Food (estimate)
- Mid-range solo budget about €45-70 per day.
  - Breakfast: €5-8.
  - Lunch prix fixe or bistro: €16-25.
  - Dinner: €25-40.
  - Coffee and extras: €5-10.

## Paris to Rome on 2027-09-08 (from memory, unverified)
- **Flight**: about 2 h 10 min gate to gate. Airlines: Air France, ITA, easyJet, Vueling, Transavia, Ryanair (from Beauvais, a poor choice). Typical fare €50-150 one way, booked early. Allow transfer time to the airport and check-in, so door to door is about 5-6 h. From CDG, the RER B takes 35-50 min. Arrival is at FCO.
- **Train**: no direct train. The Paris to Milan TGV was about 7 h, then a Milan to Rome Frecciarossa about 3 h. Total is about 11-12 h with a connection, so I would not recommend it. Sleeper options have been unreliable. Verify.
- **Recommendation (inference)**: take a morning or midday flight.

## Rome

### Where to stay (inference)
- **Centro Storico (near Pantheon, Piazza Navona, Campo de' Fiori)**: walkable and atmospheric. Metro is not close, but buses and walking work.
- **Monti**: central, local feel, near the Colosseum, and Cavour metro (Line B).
- **Prati (near the Vatican)**: calm, safe, good for the Vatican, with Ottaviano and Lepanto on Metro A.
- **Trastevere**: charming and lively, noisy at night, and less well connected by Metro (trams and buses only).
- **Avoid for a solo stay**: the area around Termini at night is OK for transit but sketchy. Pickpockets are common on Metro A and bus 64, and around the Colosseum and Trevi.
- Hotel mid-range guess: €130-220 per night.

### Attractions (from memory, verify)
| Sight | Approx. price | Closed | Booking |
|---|---|---|---|
| Colosseum + Forum + Palatine | About €18-24 (the "full experience" with arena or underground costs more) | Open daily | **Timed entry, book ahead, often sold out weeks ahead.** Tickets are name-bound. |
| Vatican Museums + Sistine Chapel | About €20-25 online (€17 + €5 booking fee historically) | **Sundays** (except the last Sunday of the month, free but crowded) | Book ahead. Sunday 2027-09-12 is not the last Sunday, so closed. |
| St. Peter's Basilica | Free (dome about €10-13) | Open daily; may close for papal events | Security queue. Dress code covers knees and shoulders |
| Borghese Gallery | About €15 + €2 fee | **Monday** | **Compulsory timed 2-hour slot, book weeks ahead** |
| Pantheon | About €5 (introduced in 2023) | Open daily | Same-day ticket is OK |
| Trevi Fountain | A visitor fee was planned (about €2) from 2026. **Unconfirmed** | | |
- Rome is full of other attractions (Capitoline Museums, Castel Sant'Angelo, Catacombs). Details not checked.
- **Schedule note (inference)**: 2027-09-12 is a Sunday, so the Vatican Museums are closed. 2027-09-13 is a Monday, so the Borghese is closed. Weekday for other dates: Sept 4 is Saturday, Sept 8 is Wednesday. The Louvre is closed Tuesday, 2027-09-07, and Orsay is closed Monday, 2027-09-06. (Weekdays are computed from the calendar. Good confidence.)

### Transfers and transit (from memory)
- **FCO to centre**:
  - Leonardo Express to Termini: about €14, 32 min.
  - Regional FL1 train: about €8, to Trastevere/Ostiense.
  - Fixed-fare taxi: about €55 inside the Aurelian Walls.
  - Airport bus: €6-7.
- **Transit**:
  - Single BIT ticket: €1.50 for 100 min.
  - 24 h: about €7.
  - 48 h: about €12.50.
  - 72 h: about €18.
  - Weekly: about €24.
  - Contactless bank-card tap is being rolled out on the Metro. Unconfirmed.
- **Tourist tax**: charged per person per night, paid at the hotel. Mid-range hotels (3-4 star) pay roughly €6-7.50 per night, up to 10 nights. 5-star pays about €10. Rates were stable as of my memory. Check for any 2027 change.

### Food (estimate)
- Mid-range solo budget about €40-65 per day.
  - Breakfast (cappuccino and cornetto): €3-5.
  - Lunch (pizza al taglio or trattoria): €12-20.
  - Dinner: €25-40.
  - Coperto (cover charge) €1-3 is common. Avoid tourist-trap menus near the main sights.

## Weather and crowds (general knowledge)
- **Paris early Sept**: highs about 22-24°C, lows about 12-14°C, some rain. Pleasant. Crowds are still high, though a bit lower than in July and Aug.
- **Rome early Sept**: highs about 28-30°C, can reach 33°C. Warm, with occasional thunderstorms. Take a water bottle (public nasoni fountains). Crowds are lower than in August but still heavy at the major sights.

## Events and closures in early Sept 2027
- **Nothing confirmed.** I searched nothing. Things to check:
  - Paris: Journées du Patrimoine (Heritage Days) is usually the third weekend of September (Sept 18-19, 2027, after your visit). Fashion Week and trade fairs can push hotel prices up in early September.
  - Rome: possible papal or Vatican events. The Jubilee (2025) is over.
  - Strikes: French transport strikes are common, so check closer to travel.
  - Louvre has had construction and strike disruptions, and the "Louvre Nouvelle Renaissance" project may change entry. Unconfirmed.

## Inference vs. read
- **Read on a source this session:** nothing.
- **Recalled from training data, possibly stale:** all prices, closure days of the sights (long-standing patterns), transfer costs, tax rates, and EES/ETIAS dates.
- **Computed:** weekdays for the dates.
- **Pure inference:** neighbourhood recommendations, food budgets, weather ranges, itinerary notes.

# Trip options: ORD -> Paris -> Rome -> ORD, 1 adult, ECONOMY

**All results below are `source: sample-data` (synthetic, `synthetic: true`).** They are illustrative planning figures only and are not real availability or bookable offers.
Every flight and stay response carried this warning: "These are synthetic sample offers, not live availability. Prices, times, and seat/room counts are illustrative only and nothing here is bookable."

# Paris → Rome, solo, 3–13 Sep 2027

All flights and hotels below are **sample-data**: illustrative, not bookable. Search for real fares before booking.

## Fri 3 Sep — Depart Chicago
- 15:56: ORD→CDG, Blue Corridor, 1 stop, economy (sample).

## Sat 4 Sep — Paris arrival
- About 07:35: land at CDG. Take the RER B into the city (~€14) and drop your bags at the guesthouse (Marais / Saint-Germain area preferred).
- Easy day against jet lag: walk the Marais, Place des Vosges, then a Seine walk at dusk.

## Sun 5 Sep — Louvre
- Morning: Louvre, with a timed ticket booked ahead (~€22). Then the Tuileries and Palais-Royal.
- Afternoon/evening: Saint-Germain cafés.

## Mon 6 Sep — Île de la Cité and Eiffel (Orsay is closed Mondays)
- Morning: Sainte-Chapelle (timed ticket, ~€14), Notre-Dame and the Latin Quarter.
- Evening: Eiffel Tower summit at sunset (book ahead, ~€38), then Trocadéro.

## Tue 7 Sep — Orsay and Montmartre (Louvre is closed Tuesdays)
- Morning: Musée d'Orsay (~€17).
- Afternoon/evening: Montmartre and Sacré-Cœur.

## Wed 8 Sep — To Rome
- Morning: get to Orly. 12:19: ORY→FCO, Northwind (sample).
- Afternoon: Leonardo Express to Termini (~€14), then check in (Monti / Centro Storico preferred).
- Evening: Trevi Fountain and dinner in Monti.

## Thu 9 Sep — Ancient Rome
- Colosseum, Roman Forum and Palatine on a timed ticket (~€18–24, book weeks ahead). Afternoon rest in the heat; evening on the Capitoline.

## Fri 10 Sep — Vatican
- Morning: Vatican Museums and the Sistine Chapel (book ahead, ~€20–25), then St Peter's Basilica.
- Afternoon: Prati, Castel Sant'Angelo from outside.

## Sat 11 Sep — Borghese and Centro Storico
- Morning: Borghese Gallery, timed entry booked ahead (~€17).
- Afternoon: Spanish Steps, Pantheon, Piazza Navona.

## Sun 12 Sep — Trastevere (Vatican Museums closed)
- Campo de' Fiori, Trastevere, sunset from the Gianicolo. A good day for the discretionary budget (food tour, Ostia Antica).

## Mon 13 Sep — Fly home (Borghese closed)
- Free morning. Take the Leonardo Express to FCO. 19:34: FCO→ORD, Meridian Air, 1 stop (sample).

## Before booking
- ETIAS/EES rules for 2027, every ticket price, transit fares, tourist-tax rates, and early-Sep 2027 events and strikes were **not checked online**. The research tool had no web access, so these figures are from memory.
- Book the Vatican, Colosseum, Borghese, Louvre and Eiffel tickets as soon as their sale windows open.

# Traveler profile
- Home airport: Chicago O'Hare (ORD)
- Travels solo (at least sometimes)
- Cabin preference: not yet stated (economy used by default)

- Sep 2027: Paris → Rome, 10 days, solo (planned Nov 2026)

tool_results.content:
**I had no web search or browsing tool, so nothing in the file was checked against a live source.** Everything in `/trip/research.md` comes from my memory of older information, so prices and rules may be out of date by Sept 2027. The file marks this throughout.

**Topics not searched or confirmed:**
- Current ticket prices.
- 2027 events and closures.
- ETIAS and EES status.
- Transit fares.
- Taxi and train fares.
- Tourist-tax rates.
- Weather.

**Weekdays (calculated from the calendar, high confidence):**
- **Dates:** Sept 4 is a Saturday, Sept 8 is a Wednesday, and Sept 13 is a Monday.
- **Paris closures:** The Louvre is closed Tuesday Sept 7, and the Musée d'Orsay is closed Monday Sept 6.
- **Rome closures:** The Vatican Museums are closed Sunday Sept 12, and the Borghese Gallery is closed Monday Sept 13. Since Sept 12 isn't the last Sunday of the month, there's no free-entry Sunday.
- **Rome on Sept 9–11:** Plan the Vatican, Colosseum and Borghese visits for Sept 9–11. That's Thursday to Saturday, when all three are open.

**Remembered figures, to verify before booking:**
- **Entry:** Americans can enter the Schengen area for up to 90 days without a visa. EES biometric registration was scheduled to start in Oct 2025. Whether ETIAS (about €7) will be required by Sept 2027 is unconfirmed, so check the official EU site about 3 months before you go.
- **Paris sights:** The Louvre is about €22 and the Eiffel Tower summit lift about €36–40. Sainte-Chapelle is about €13–15 and Orsay about €16–18. All need timed or advance booking.
- **Rome sights:** The Colosseum/Forum is about €18–24, the Vatican Museums about €20–25, and the Borghese about €17. All three need timed advance booking, often weeks ahead.
- **Airport transfers:**
  - Paris (CDG): RER B is about €13–14. A taxi is a flat €56–65.
  - Rome (FCO): the Leonardo Express train is about €14. A taxi is a fixed €55.
- **Transit passes:**
  - Paris: A weekly Navigo pass only runs Monday to Sunday, so it's poor value for your stay. Use a carnet of tickets instead.
  - Rome: A 72-hour pass is about €18.
- **Paris to Rome on Sept 8:** Fly, which takes about 2 h 10 min and costs roughly €50–150. The train needs a change in Milan and takes about 11–12 hours, so I wouldn't recommend it.
- **Food per day:** About €45–70 in Paris and €40–65 in Rome.
- **Tourist tax:** Paris is about €3–5 per night at a 3–4 star hotel. Rome is about €6–7.50 per night at a 3–4 star hotel.
- **Weather:** Paris is around 22–24°C and mild. Rome is around 28–30°C, with possible storms. Crowds are still heavy in both.

**Neighbourhoods:**
- **Paris:** Le Marais or Saint-Germain/Latin Quarter. This is my own judgement, not from a source.
- **Rome:** Monti, the Centro Storico, or Prati. This is also my own judgement.

**Not confirmed at all:** early-Sept 2027 events, strikes, Louvre changes, a possible Trevi Fountain fee, and any 2026 or 2027 price changes.

I wrote the candidates to `/trip/options.md`. Every result, flights and lodging, has `source: sample-data` (synthetic). These are illustrative planning figures, not live availability, and none of them can be booked. Each response also carried the sample-data `warning`.

- **Cabin:** every flight came back as economy, and there was no `cabin_note`.
- **Expiry:** sample offers have no `expires_at` or `expires_in_seconds`.
- **Bag fees:** no checked-bag costs were shown, so they are unknown.
- **Multi-city:** the search tool has no multi-city mode, so I priced the trip as separate one-ways.
- **Neighbourhoods:** the stay results have no neighbourhood field, so I couldn't confirm Marais, Saint-Germain, Monti or similar.
- **Lodging amounts:** no stay returned a `due_at_accommodation` amount, so `total_cost` is the only figure.
- **Cancellation:** every stay stated its `free_cancellation` value, so none was unknown.

**Cheapest (USD, all sample-data)**
- **Flights, $1,505.76:**
  - ORD→CDG on Anser Airways, 2 stops: $692.98.
  - ORY→FCO on Blue Corridor, 2 stops: $367.44.
  - FCO→ORD on Northwind, 2 stops: $445.34.
  - The Anser outbound probably arrives on 9/3, which would need an extra hotel night.
- **Lodging, $1,497.19:**
  - Paris private-room hostel: $770.44 total, rated 7.8, not refundable.
  - Rome private-room hostel: $726.75 total, rated 7.8, not refundable.
- **Total: $3,002.95.**

**Most convenient (USD, all sample-data)**
- **Flights, $2,273.04, all nonstop:**
  - ORD→CDG on Meridian Air, departs 18:10, arrives about 08:45 on 9/4: $1,078.92.
  - ORY→FCO on Anser Airways, departs 09:33: $570.76.
  - FCO→ORD on Anser Airways, departs 18:27: $623.36.
- **Lodging, $2,923.35:** central boutique hotels, rated 8.9, not refundable (Paris $1,494.60, Rome $1,428.75).
- **Total: $5,196.39.** This is over budget.

**Tradeoff**
- Going from cheapest to most convenient adds about $2,200, mostly from nonstop fares and boutique hotels.
- ORY→FCO is much cheaper than CDG→FCO, which starts at $656.90.
- A plain ORD–CDG round trip is cheaper on paper, from $598.68. It doesn't fit the route, because it returns from Paris and would need an unpriced Rome→Paris leg.

**Recommendation (sample-data, $3,269.11 total)**
- **Flights, $1,586.88, 1 stop each:**
  - ORD→CDG on Blue Corridor, departs 15:56, arrives about 07:35 on 9/4: $740.99.
  - ORY→FCO on Northwind, departs 12:19: $379.72.
  - FCO→ORD on Meridian Air, departs 19:34: $466.17.
- **Paris:** quiet guesthouse, $955.48 total ($238.87 a night), rated 9.1, free cancellation.
- **Rome:** private-room hostel, $726.75 total ($145.35 a night), rated 7.8, not refundable.
- If you can stretch about $78 past the $3,300 cap, use the cheapest flights ($1,505.76) with guesthouses in both cities. The Rome guesthouse is $917.25, rated 9.1, with free cancellation. That comes to $3,378.49.
- Bag fees would add to either total. Both are well inside the $5,000 overall budget.

# Paris (2027-09-04 to 09-08) and Rome (2027-09-08 to 09-13): research notes

## READ THIS FIRST: provenance
- **No web search or browsing tool was available in this session.** I only had file tools. Nothing below was verified against a live source.
- Everything is **from my background knowledge (training data), not read on a source today (2026-11-04)**. Prices and rules are probably 1-3 years old and may have changed by Sept 2027.
- Every figure is an estimate to re-check on the official site before booking.
- Failed or not done, every topic: all web searches. Topics that needed searching: current ticket prices, 2027 events and closures, ETIAS/EES status, Paris and Rome transit fares, taxi and transfer fares, train and flight prices, tourist tax rates, weather. None of these were confirmed.

## Entry requirements (US passport), unverified
- Schengen area: France and Italy both. 90 days in 180 without a visa. Passport should be valid 3+ months beyond departure. Ideally have 6 months.
- **EES (Entry/Exit System)**: biometric registration at the border. Its launch was scheduled for 12 Oct 2025 with a phased rollout over about 6 months. Under that plan it should be live by Sept 2027. **Not confirmed.** Expect fingerprint and photo at first entry, and possible queues.
- **ETIAS**: about €7 online authorisation for visa-exempt travelers. It was expected to start in the last quarter of 2026. Delays are common. **Whether it will be required by Sept 2027 is unconfirmed.** Check travel-europe.europa.eu/etias and the US State Department pages about 3 months before departure. Use official sites only, because look-alike scam sites exist.

## Paris

### Where to stay (inference from general knowledge)
- **Le Marais (3rd/4th)**: central, walkable, lively, good food. Metro lines 1, 11, 8, 9.
- **Saint-Germain-des-Prés / Latin Quarter (5th/6th)**: classic, safe, restaurants. Metro 4, 10, 12. RER B at Saint-Michel and Luxembourg.
- **Île Saint-Louis / Louvre-Tuileries (1st)**: central, pricier.
- **Avoid for a solo first visit**: areas around Gare du Nord, Gare de l'Est, Barbès and Pigalle at night. They are fine for transit but can feel rough late. Pickpockets are common at the Eiffel Tower, Louvre, Metro line 1 and Montmartre.
- Mid-range hotel rate guess: €150-250 per night in September. Sept is busy (rentrée, trade fairs), so book early.

### Attractions: prices and closures (from memory, verify)
| Sight | Approx. price | Closed | Booking |
|---|---|---|---|
| Louvre | €22 (rose to about €22 in 2024; a non-EU surcharge was discussed for 2026, unconfirmed) | **Tuesday** | Timed slot required, book ahead |
| Eiffel Tower | Lift to summit about €36-40, stairs to 2nd floor about €13-15 | Open daily | Book weeks ahead. Tickets release about 60 days out |
| Sainte-Chapelle | About €13-15 | Open daily | Timed slot recommended |
| Musée d'Orsay | About €16-18 | **Monday** | Book ahead |
| Notre-Dame (cathedral) | Free | Open daily | Reopened Dec 2024. Optional free reservation to skip the queue |
| Versailles (if added) | Palace about €21-32 | **Monday** | Timed ticket. Château closes Mondays |
| Arc de Triomphe top | About €16 | Open daily | Book ahead |
- The Musée d'Orsay and Louvre may have ticket rules or hours that have changed. Check the official sites.
- Sunday free-entry rules (e.g. first Sunday of the month at some museums) have been changing. Unconfirmed.

### Transfers and transit (from memory)
- **CDG to centre**:
  - RER B: about €13-14, 35-50 min. The fare rose in 2024-25. Verify.
  - Taxi flat rate: about €56 (Right Bank) or €65 (Left Bank).
  - Roissybus: about €16-17.
  - Late arrival: RER B has security issues at night, and works sometimes cut service.
- **Transit**:
  - Single Metro ticket: about €2.50. The price rose in 2025 to about €2.50 (€2.55 on cards).
  - Navigo Easy card: about €2 for the card. Carnets of 10 are cheaper per ride.
  - **Navigo Decouverte weekly**: about €32 and valid **Monday to Sunday only**. Poor value for a Saturday to Wednesday stay.
  - Paris Visite pass: pricier. Likely worse than individual tickets for a moderate-pace stay.
  - Most sights are within walkable or 1-2 Metro-ride range, so budget about €10-15 total on rides.
- **Taxe de séjour**: charged by the hotel per person per night. For 3-4 star hotels roughly €3-5 per night, including the regional surcharge. The 2025 rise was reported but not confirmed.

### Food (estimate)
- Mid-range solo budget about €45-70 per day.
  - Breakfast: €5-8.
  - Lunch prix fixe or bistro: €16-25.
  - Dinner: €25-40.
  - Coffee and extras: €5-10.

## Paris to Rome on 2027-09-08 (from memory, unverified)
- **Flight**: about 2 h 10 min gate to gate. Airlines: Air France, ITA, easyJet, Vueling, Transavia, Ryanair (from Beauvais, a poor choice). Typical fare €50-150 one way, booked early. Allow transfer time to the airport and check-in, so door to door is about 5-6 h. From CDG, the RER B takes 35-50 min. Arrival is at FCO.
- **Train**: no direct train. The Paris to Milan TGV was about 7 h, then a Milan to Rome Frecciarossa about 3 h. Total is about 11-12 h with a connection, so I would not recommend it. Sleeper options have been unreliable. Verify.
- **Recommendation (inference)**: take a morning or midday flight.

## Rome

### Where to stay (inference)
- **Centro Storico (near Pantheon, Piazza Navona, Campo de' Fiori)**: walkable and atmospheric. Metro is not close, but buses and walking work.
- **Monti**: central, local feel, near the Colosseum, and Cavour metro (Line B).
- **Prati (near the Vatican)**: calm, safe, good for the Vatican, with Ottaviano and Lepanto on Metro A.
- **Trastevere**: charming and lively, noisy at night, and less well connected by Metro (trams and buses only).
- **Avoid for a solo stay**: the area around Termini at night is OK for transit but sketchy. Pickpockets are common on Metro A and bus 64, and around the Colosseum and Trevi.
- Hotel mid-range guess: €130-220 per night.

### Attractions (from memory, verify)
| Sight | Approx. price | Closed | Booking |
|---|---|---|---|
| Colosseum + Forum + Palatine | About €18-24 (the "full experience" with arena or underground costs more) | Open daily | **Timed entry, book ahead, often sold out weeks ahead.** Tickets are name-bound. |
| Vatican Museums + Sistine Chapel | About €20-25 online (€17 + €5 booking fee historically) | **Sundays** (except the last Sunday of the month, free but crowded) | Book ahead. Sunday 2027-09-12 is not the last Sunday, so closed. |
| St. Peter's Basilica | Free (dome about €10-13) | Open daily; may close for papal events | Security queue. Dress code covers knees and shoulders |
| Borghese Gallery | About €15 + €2 fee | **Monday** | **Compulsory timed 2-hour slot, book weeks ahead** |
| Pantheon | About €5 (introduced in 2023) | Open daily | Same-day ticket is OK |
| Trevi Fountain | A visitor fee was planned (about €2) from 2026. **Unconfirmed** | | |
- Rome is full of other attractions (Capitoline Museums, Castel Sant'Angelo, Catacombs). Details not checked.
- **Schedule note (inference)**: 2027-09-12 is a Sunday, so the Vatican Museums are closed. 2027-09-13 is a Monday, so the Borghese is closed. Weekday for other dates: Sept 4 is Saturday, Sept 8 is Wednesday. The Louvre is closed Tuesday, 2027-09-07, and Orsay is closed Monday, 2027-09-06. (Weekdays are computed from the calendar. Good confidence.)

### Transfers and transit (from memory)
- **FCO to centre**:
  - Leonardo Express to Termini: about €14, 32 min.
  - Regional FL1 train: about €8, to Trastevere/Ostiense.
  - Fixed-fare taxi: about €55 inside the Aurelian Walls.
  - Airport bus: €6-7.
- **Transit**:
  - Single BIT ticket: €1.50 for 100 min.
  - 24 h: about €7.
  - 48 h: about €12.50.
  - 72 h: about €18.
  - Weekly: about €24.
  - Contactless bank-card tap is being rolled out on the Metro. Unconfirmed.
- **Tourist tax**: charged per person per night, paid at the hotel. Mid-range hotels (3-4 star) pay roughly €6-7.50 per night, up to 10 nights. 5-star pays about €10. Rates were stable as of my memory. Check for any 2027 change.

### Food (estimate)
- Mid-range solo budget about €40-65 per day.
  - Breakfast (cappuccino and cornetto): €3-5.
  - Lunch (pizza al taglio or trattoria): €12-20.
  - Dinner: €25-40.
  - Coperto (cover charge) €1-3 is common. Avoid tourist-trap menus near the main sights.

## Weather and crowds (general knowledge)
- **Paris early Sept**: highs about 22-24°C, lows about 12-14°C, some rain. Pleasant. Crowds are still high, though a bit lower than in July and Aug.
- **Rome early Sept**: highs about 28-30°C, can reach 33°C. Warm, with occasional thunderstorms. Take a water bottle (public nasoni fountains). Crowds are lower than in August but still heavy at the major sights.

## Events and closures in early Sept 2027
- **Nothing confirmed.** I searched nothing. Things to check:
  - Paris: Journées du Patrimoine (Heritage Days) is usually the third weekend of September (Sept 18-19, 2027, after your visit). Fashion Week and trade fairs can push hotel prices up in early September.
  - Rome: possible papal or Vatican events. The Jubilee (2025) is over.
  - Strikes: French transport strikes are common, so check closer to travel.
  - Louvre has had construction and strike disruptions, and the "Louvre Nouvelle Renaissance" project may change entry. Unconfirmed.

## Inference vs. read
- **Read on a source this session:** nothing.
- **Recalled from training data, possibly stale:** all prices, closure days of the sights (long-standing patterns), transfer costs, tax rates, and EES/ETIAS dates.
- **Computed:** weekdays for the dates.
- **Pure inference:** neighbourhood recommendations, food budgets, weather ranges, itinerary notes.

# Paris → Rome, solo, 3–13 Sep 2027

All flights and hotels below are **sample-data**: illustrative, not bookable. Search for real fares before booking.

## Fri 3 Sep — Depart Chicago
- 15:56: ORD→CDG, Blue Corridor, 1 stop, economy (sample).

## Sat 4 Sep — Paris arrival
- About 07:35: land at CDG. Take the RER B into the city (~€14) and drop your bags at the guesthouse (Marais / Saint-Germain area preferred).
- Easy day against jet lag: walk the Marais, Place des Vosges, then a Seine walk at dusk.

## Sun 5 Sep — Louvre
- Morning: Louvre, with a timed ticket booked ahead (~€22). Then the Tuileries and Palais-Royal.
- Afternoon/evening: Saint-Germain cafés.

## Mon 6 Sep — Île de la Cité and Eiffel (Orsay is closed Mondays)
- Morning: Sainte-Chapelle (timed ticket, ~€14), Notre-Dame and the Latin Quarter.
- Evening: Eiffel Tower summit at sunset (book ahead, ~€38), then Trocadéro.

## Tue 7 Sep — Orsay and Montmartre (Louvre is closed Tuesdays)
- Morning: Musée d'Orsay (~€17).
- Afternoon/evening: Montmartre and Sacré-Cœur.

## Wed 8 Sep — To Rome
- Morning: get to Orly. 12:19: ORY→FCO, Northwind (sample).
- Afternoon: Leonardo Express to Termini (~€14), then check in (Monti / Centro Storico preferred).
- Evening: Trevi Fountain and dinner in Monti.

## Thu 9 Sep — Ancient Rome
- Colosseum, Roman Forum and Palatine on a timed ticket (~€18–24, book weeks ahead). Afternoon rest in the heat; evening on the Capitoline.

## Fri 10 Sep — Vatican
- Morning: Vatican Museums and the Sistine Chapel (book ahead, ~€20–25), then St Peter's Basilica.
- Afternoon: Prati, Castel Sant'Angelo from outside.

## Sat 11 Sep — Borghese and Centro Storico
- Morning: Borghese Gallery, timed entry booked ahead (~€17).
- Afternoon: Spanish Steps, Pantheon, Piazza Navona.

## Sun 12 Sep — Trastevere (Vatican Museums closed)
- Campo de' Fiori, Trastevere, sunset from the Gianicolo. A good day for the discretionary budget (food tour, Ostia Antica).

## Mon 13 Sep — Fly home (Borghese closed)
- Free morning. Take the Leonardo Express to FCO. 19:34: FCO→ORD, Meridian Air, 1 stop (sample).

## Before booking
- ETIAS/EES rules for 2027, every ticket price, transit fares, tourist-tax rates, and early-Sep 2027 events and strikes were **not checked online**. The research tool had no web access, so these figures are from memory.
- Book the Vatican, Colosseum, Borghese, Louvre and Eiffel tickets as soon as their sale windows open.
